pages.title: INTRODUCTION
pages.text: INTRODUCTION This document, Special Provisions and Standard Drawings for the Installation and Modification of Traffic Signals, governs the contractual construction activities related to traffic signals in the City of Los Angeles. Where no contract is applicable, but reference is made to “contractor”, said provisions apply to the City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation field forces. This edition supersedes all previous editions. This document supplements the Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction, or “Green book”, as adopted by the City of Los Angeles Board of Public Works and as modified by the corresponding issue of the “Brown Book.” Together, all of these documents govern all contractual construction activities. All materials used in the installation and/or modification of traffic signal systems shall conform to the latest Material Specification of the City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation. The LADOT Material Specifications may be obtained from the Material Services Division, Department of Transportation, 100 South Main Street, 10th Floor, Los Angeles, California, 90012, telephone number (213) 928-9636 or can be downloaded in PDF format from the LADOT web site at: http://www.ladot.lacity.org/tf_Development_Review.htm. 1

pages.title: PART I
pages.text: PART I SPECIAL PROVISIONS A. GENERAL 1. DEFINITIONS ATSAC: Automated Traffic Surveillance and Control. LABPW: City of Los Angeles Board of Public Works. LADOT: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation MUTCD: Manual of Uniform Traffic Control Devices (California Supplement) WATCH: Work Area Traffic Control Handbook 2. LADOT DISTRICT FIELD OPERATIONS YARD The address and telephone numbers of the LADOT Field Operations Yards are listed below: Valley Yard: 14832 Raymer Street, Van Nuys; (818) 756-7845 Central Yard: 1831 Pasadena Ave, Los Angeles; (213) 485-7689 • • • Western Yard: 2801 Exposition Blvd, Los Angeles; (213) 485-6818 3. PURCHASE OF THIS DOCUMENT This document, Special Provisions and Standard Drawings for the Installation and Modification of Traffic Signals, may be purchased from the LADOT Records Section, 100 South Main Street, 10th Floor, Los Angeles, California, 90012, telephone number (213) 972­ 5060. This document can also be downloaded in PDF format from the LADOT web site at: http://www.ladot.lacity.org/tf_Development_Review.htm 4. MATERIAL All materials used in the installation and/or modification of non-temporary signal systems shall be new and unused, unless otherwise specified on the plan and shall conform to the latest LADOT Material Specifications. Temporary signal standards and signal heads installed on these standards may be used, but shall be undamaged. 2

pages.title: 5. NOTIFICATION
pages.text: 5. NOTIFICATION The contractor shall notify LADOT Traffic Signal Inspector at Central Yard, (213) 485-1071, Valley Yard, (818) 756-7852, or Western Yard, (213) 485-6834, depending on the project location, five (5) working days prior to start of construction on any project involving work on traffic signals or signal systems. In case of emergency, the LADOT Traffic Signal Inspector may authorize requests for change orders. The signal inspector shall be notified for inspection approval of all underground substructures, including foundations, 48 hours prior to covering the work or pouring foundations. Any work that will affect a major ATSAC communication facility (i.e. fiber optic cable, main communication trunk cable, communication hub site, etc.) as determined by the LADOT Traffic Signal Inspector, shall be prohibited between the hours of 6:00 A.M. to 9:00 A.M. and 3:00 P.M. to 7:00 P.M. on weekdays, except national holidays. If such work requires that ATSAC communication system be off line for five (5) or more working days during the hours permitted, the contractor shall provide temporary facilities in order to maintain operation of the ATSAC system. These temporary facilities may include, but are not limited to, overhead spans of fiber optic or communication cable, and any related equipment. Any work required to install and remove these temporary facilities shall be done at the contractor’s expense. Once said temporary facilities are in place, the contractor shall have thirty (30) working days in which to complete construction and to fully restore the ATSAC communication system. Failure to notify the LADOT Traffic Signal Inspector prior to start of work will result in suspension of work. Delays in the complete restoration of the signal system may require the contractor to pay liquidated damages as specified in the contract or may require LADOT forces to complete the work which will be charged to the contractor and/or permittee. Traffic control shall be in accordance with the LADOT Standard Plan S-488.0, the latest edition of the WATCH manual, MUTCD (California Supplement), associated worksite traffic control plans or any additional requirements called for on the plan or in the special provisions. 6. WORKSITE TRAFFIC CONTROL The contractor shall install and maintain overhead cable or wires to maintain existing signal operation when installing new conduit runs across the street, replacing cable runs across the street, or installing or replacing signal standards, foundations or heads. Regular traffic signal control (including interconnect) shall be maintained from 6:00 A.M. to 9:00 A.M. and 3:00 P.M. to 7:00 P.M. on weekdays, except national holidays. National holidays are New Year’s Day, President’s Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Veteran’s Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas. Flashing, activation and deactivation of signals and interconnect may occur only between 9:00 A.M. and 3:00 P.M. and between 7:00 P.M. and 6:00 A.M. on weekdays, except national holidays, and shall be accomplished only by an LADOT traffic signal electrician. The LADOT traffic signal electrician may reschedule or cancel a scheduled signal deactivation in the event of unsafe working or weather conditions. Arrangements to deactivate signals (signal shutdown) shall be made at least 24 hours in advance, Monday-Thursday at (213) 473-8478 before 9:00 A.M. on non-holiday weekdays. The LADOT project number as shown on the traffic signal plan must be given at this time. The contractor may be charged for electrical and traffic control work provided by LADOT. 3

pages.title: 7. CONTRACTOR REQUIREMENTS
pages.text: 7. CONTRACTOR REQUIREMENTS All traffic signal and/or related electrical work shall be performed and inspected under the conditions of the most current, amended Board of Public Works “Enhanced Electrical Safety Policy”. The “Enhanced Electrical Safety Policy” is applicable for all work on traffic signals and/or related electrical work performed for LADOT regardless of contract cost. The Contractor shall certify that all personnel employed in traffic signal and/or related work fully comply with the requirements of the “Enhanced Electrical Safety Policy”. Failure to fully comply with the requirements of the “Enhanced Electrical Safety Policy” may result in a suspension of work and/or sanctions against the Contractor. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL NOT WORK ON TRAFFIC SIGNAL CIRCUITS WHILE THEY ARE ENERGIZED When a signal shutdown is approved by LADOT, it shall be two (2) hours maximum, unless approved for a longer period, and may occur only between the hours of 9A.M. to 3P.M. Monday-Thursday on non-holiday weekdays. The Traffic Signal Inspector may authorize work necessitating longer periods of time. Preliminary work associated with the signal shutdown shall be done prior to the actual shutdown in order to minimize the amount of time necessary for the completion of the work. Sufficient staffing and equipment shall be employed by the contractor to minimize the shutdown period. Once a shutdown is affected, all work shall be diligently pursued without interruption until the signals are back in normal operation. 8. TRAFFIC CONTROL SIGNING Any traffic control signing damaged or lost by the contractor shall be replaced at the contractor's expense. Arrangements for obtaining replacement signing (with subsequent billing) shall be made with the LADOT Bureau of Accounting, General Accounting Division, at (213) 972-5908. Prior to the completion of construction, the contractor shall permanently mount all traffic control signing per LADOT standards. Five (5) working days prior to any traffic signal pole removal, the appropriate yard Superintendent shall be notified for the removal and reinstallation of pole and mast arm mounted street name signs. The address and phone numbers of the LADOT Field Operations Yards are shown in Section 2. 9. LADOT SUPPLIED MATERIAL Arrangements for obtaining materials, except traffic signal controller assemblies, to be supplied by LADOT as indicated on traffic signal design plans, shall be made ten (10) working days in advance by contacting the LADOT Field Operations Division at (213) 928­ 9620. 4

pages.title: 10. CONTROLLER TESTING
pages.text: 10. CONTROLLER TESTING All traffic signal controller assemblies being furnished and installed by the contractor must be tested by LADOT. The completely assembled controller with cabinet and auxiliary equipment shall be delivered to the LADOT Traffic Signal Shop at Piper Technical Center, 555 Ramirez Street, Los Angeles, California, 90012, telephone number (213) 473-8468, at least thirty (30) working days prior to desired pick-up date. The traffic signal program for the Model 2070 controller will be supplied and installed by LADOT. Upon successful completion of the testing, the contractor shall pick up the traffic signal controller assemblies within fifteen (15) working days after notification for installation at the job site. 11. SALVAGE EQUIPMENT All arrangements for traffic signal equipment specified to be returned to LADOT shall be made five (5) working days prior to the desired delivery date. Controller cabinets shall become the property of the contractor, unless indicated otherwise on the project plans or by the LADOT Traffic Signal Inspector. The model 170 or 2070 controller units, model 210 or 2010 conflict monitor and specialized equipment, as determined by the LADOT Traffic Signal Inspector, contained within the cabinet remain the property of LADOT and will be removed from the controller cabinet by the LADOT Traffic Signal Inspector. Return controller cabinets to the following location: LADOT Equipment Repair Shop 447 Ducommun St, Los Angeles, California, 90012 Telephone: (213) 847-2944 The contractor shall exercise due care in the removal of traffic signal equipment, including signs and sign posts, that have been specified to be reused or salvaged, so that the equipment will remain in the same condition as that prior to removal. The contractor will be required to replace any traffic signal equipment that was damaged or destroyed while in the contractor's care. The contractor shall be responsible for cleaning traffic signal equipment prior to delivery. 5

pages.title: B. CONSTRUCTION PRACTICES
pages.text: B. CONSTRUCTION PRACTICES 1. PULL BOXES The tops of pull boxes installed in the sidewalk areas shall be flush with the surrounding grade or the top of the adjacent curb. Where practical, pull boxes adjacent to standards shall be placed with a clearance of three (3) feet from the side of foundations. Pull boxes shall not be placed in curb ramp areas or driveways. Pull boxes shall be located beyond the door opening paths of traffic signal controllers. Unless physically impractical, pull boxes shall be installed at least six (6) inches from any substructure or back of curb. This is to allow for rock under and cement around the pull box. Type PB-3 pull boxes shall be used for all: a. Interconnect runs (telephone and/or fiber optic cables) b. Power service conduits c. Controllers d. Junctions with four or more conduits e. Junctions with three conduits, two of which are three-inch in diameter f. All street crossings Type PB-2 pull boxes shall be installed at all other locations, unless otherwise noted on the plans. The service pull box shall be separated from the intersection wiring whenever possible. For fiber optic runs, the spacing between the pull boxes shall be at intervals not to exceed 600 feet. For all other runs, pull boxes shall be spaced at intervals not to exceed 300 feet. Existing pull boxes are considered to be an integral part of the surrounding concrete sidewalk. Where the surrounding sidewalk surface is composed of a special material, pull boxes with covers of compatible material shall be used to obtain a homogeneous appearance of the sidewalk area. The contractor shall be required to replace the pull boxes when modifying or replacing the surrounding concrete. Replacement of pull boxes shall be made per LADOT Standard Drawing S-78.5.3 or S-78.8. Under no circumstances is any pull box to be reused or modified for reuse. 2. CONDUIT a. Material Rigid non-metallic conduits conforming to the requirements in UL Publication 651 for Rigid Non-metallic Conduit (PVC Schedule 80) shall be used, except where galvanized rigid steel conduit is required or permitted. Galvanized rigid steel conduit shall be used where specified in this manual, where shown on the plans, or where jacking is required. Galvanized rigid steel conduit is permitted where exposed above ground as a permanent installation or where authorized by the LADOT Traffic Signal Inspector. A separate #8 green ground wire and a Kevlar High Strength Conduit Measuring Tape, Greenlee catalog number 39243, 39244, 39245 (or equivalent), shall be 6

clean.title: Composite Pull Box, Types PB-2 & PB-3
clean.summary: Polymer concrete pull box for non-traffic areas with a non-skid polymer concrete cover marked TRAFFIC SIGNAL. Includes installation section and side view, cover details, captive bolt and threaded insert details, and a nominal dimensions table for Types PB2 and PB3. Boxes may be stacked no more than two deep.

pages.text: included within the PVC conduits at the time of installation. For the galvanized steel conduit a Kevlar High Strength Conduit Measuring Tape, Greenlee catalog number 39243, 39244, 39245 (or equivalent), shall be included. All the #8 green ground wires shall be spliced together and connected to the “equipment ground bus” bar inside the controller cabinet. b. Trenching PVC conduit shall be installed in open soil trenches and in pavement trenches whose edges have been saw cut, except in the vicinity of pull boxes where it may be bored in pre-drilled, augured or air-blown holes. Generally, trenches should be four inches wide. Where trenching occurs within Portland Cement Concrete, a 24-inch wide section of roadbed whose edges have been saw cut shall be removed. Trenching is not permitted through Portland Cement Concrete structures, such as bus pads, spandrels and cross gutters. Where these are encountered, jacking with galvanized rigid steel conduit, or boring with PVC conduit is required. Traffic signal conduits shall be separated from street lighting conduits. New conduit runs shall be of the same size and material throughout the run. Empty PVC conduit (conduit only) shall include a #8 green ground wire and a Kevlar High Strength Conduit Measuring Tape, Greenlee catalog number 39243, 39244, 39245 (or equivalent). Empty galvanized rigid steel conduit (conduit only) shall include Kevlar High Strength Conduit Measuring Tape, Greenlee catalog number 39243, 39244, 39245 (or equivalent). Existing underground conduit being incorporated into a new system shall be cleaned with a mandrel or cylindrical wire brush and blown out with compressed air. c. Installation in Roadways Interconnect, fiber optic, system and bus detector loop conduits shall be installed at a consistent depth throughout a block with minimum cover of 18 inches (below the established edge of the gutters) on Major and Secondary highways, and 15 inches on all other streets or alleys, unless otherwise specified on the Plans. Conduits containing traffic signal load wires (115 volts) shall be installed at a consistent depth, with the minimum and maximum depths as per Section 307-2.5 of the Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction. All street crossings shall be installed at 30-inch depth. Conduit trenches approximately four (4) inches wide may be excavated at locations shown on the Plans using earth saw methods. The preferred alignment is along the outer edge of an existing gutter. Where there is no gutter, the trench shall be at a distance of 36 inches from the existing or future curb face (which will accommodate the construction of a 24-inch wide gutter in the future), or as shown on the Plans. Removal and replacement of all pavement between the trench and the edge of the existing pavement shall be done at the discretion of the Engineer. 7

On Major or Secondary highways, the asphalt concrete pavement resurfacing shall conform to the Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction. On all other asphalt concrete streets or alleys, the upper three inches of trench shall be completed with material matching the existing pavement. Major and Secondary Highways are shown on the Streets and Highways Designation map. Portland Cement Concrete (PCC) roadway resurfacing shall be a minimum of six (6) inches thick and twenty-four (24) inches wide for all classifications of roadway. Concrete pavement serving as bus pads, spandrels, cross gutters or local depressions shall not be cut. In addition, concrete curbs and gutters (regardless of gutter width) shall not be cut. At these locations, the conduit shall be bored or jacked. It is desirable to maintain a straight alignment. Routing of a conduit at a bus pad or at any other protrusions beyond the gutter edge must be approved by the Engineer. It should be noted that some installations might require locations in back of the curb. Locations where conduits are within one foot vertically and two feet horizontally from, or otherwise in conflict with, existing utilities will not be permitted. d. Backfill Backfill may be Portland Cement Concrete (PCC) when required by the Engineer, or a one-sack sand-Portland Cement slurry mix. Portland Cement Concrete backfill shall be a 520-C-2500 mix with a 4-inch maximum slump. For PCC, calcium chloride must be added up to the maximum amount allowed by Section 201-1.2.4 of the Standard Specifications. e. Installation in Parkways All conduit installations in parkways shall have a minimum cover of 16 inches below surface (LAMC Sec. 62.04). If directional bore is permitted by the Engineer, conduit depth shall have a minimum cover of 22 inches below surface. All existing improvements in parkways, including landscaping and sprinklers, shall be protected from damage or restored to pre-construction condition. f. Size All cross street conduit runs and all interconnect conduit runs between intersections, except for fiber optic interconnect runs, shall be three-inch in diameter. All fiber optic interconnect runs shall be two-inch in diameter. Three-inch conduit shall be used between an F-8 foundation and the adjacent PB-3 pull box. Two three-inch conduits are required between an F-332 foundation and the adjacent PB-3 pull box. One-inch conduit shall be used between an F-7 foundation and the adjacent pull box. All other new conduit runs shall be two-inch in diameter, unless otherwise specified on the plan. When existing conduit runs are to be modified or extended, the material and size of the new conduit shall be the same as the existing conduit. 8

pages.title: 3. BACKFILLING
pages.text: 3. BACKFILLING a. Schedule All excavations for the installation of foundations, conduits and pull boxes, and removal of old systems, shall be backfilled, compacted and restored to match adjacent areas and excess material removed from the job site within the calendar days prescribed in the following Table I. The number of days allowed commences with the start of excavation unless otherwise permitted by the Engineer. All trenching activity, commenced each day, shall be fully backfilled to the finished surface grade at the end of the day; final resurfacing shall be completed within five (5) working days. All streets and all trenches shall be maintained in safe condition until final resurfacing. b. Foundation Holes A one-sack slurry mix shall be used to backfill foundation holes created as a result of removing the existing foundations. If the area excavated for a new foundation is deemed to have unstable soil as determined by the Engineer, then the area excavated shall be backfilled with one sack slurry mix, 24 hrs prior to re-excavation for the new foundation. Where the new foundation is within three (3) feet of the existing foundation, the removal and backfill of the existing foundation shall occur prior to the installation of the new foundation. c. Trenches - See Section B.2, Conduit 9

pages.title: 4. CONDUCTORS AND CABLE
pages.text: The previous requirements do not relieve the Contractor of his/her obligation to properly place warning signs and barricades as well as maintain the job site in accordance with Subsections 7-9 and 7-10 of the Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction and the Work Area Traffic Control Handbook (WATCH) manual. If the times specified in Table I are exceeded, the Contractor (as directed by the Engineer) shall stop all other work until the restoration work is brought into compliance. Contact time will continue to be charged during such periods. Where field conditions are such that these Special Provision are conflicting, the Engineer shall be notified immediately. Where excavations occur in the sidewalks or other pedestrian ways, the Contractor shall provide a safe and orderly pedestrian passage around the excavation area. The pedestrian passage shall not subject pedestrians to hazards from traffic or construction operations, or cause pedestrians to walk upon unsuitable or hazardous surfaces. 4. CONDUCTORS AND CABLE a. Material All permanent conductors shall be run inside conduits or standards. Multi-conductor cable shall be used for all circuits in lieu of individual conductors. The multi-conductor cable shall conform to the latest revision of the following LADOT Specifications: 92-089-01 (28 conductor cable) 92-091-01 (13 conductor cable) 92-090-01 (9 conductor cable) 92-094-01 (5 conductor cable) Conductors shall be solid copper wire of the gauge shown on the plans, unless otherwise specified. Whenever new conductors are to be installed in a conduit with existing individual conductors (service wires excepted), all individual conductors shall be removed and replaced with multi-conductor cable. 28-conductor cable shall be installed in all new street crossings unless otherwise specified on the plans. Only Kevlar High Strength Conduit Measuring Tape, Greenlee catalog number 39243, 39244, 39245 (or equivalent) shall be used for "pulling in" or installing cables in ANY TYPE CONDUIT. At no time shall any type "rope" be used to install cables or wires. All temporary overhead circuit runs shall be multi-conductor cable. Where exposed over the roadway, they shall be at least 20 feet above ground. Over the sidewalk and roadside areas not open to vehicular traffic, they shall be at least 12 feet above ground. Service conductors shall have black and white insulation. 11

pages.title: 1) Wire Splicing: Where circuits are to be spliced, each splice shall be twisted
pages.text: b. Identification Each communication cable shall be identified in all communication cabinets and splice vaults by a plastic tag 1-inch by 4-inch in size, with the cable run identification characters in ½-inch letters and secured to the cable with two nylon tie-wrap devices. Each cable shall be identified in all controller cabinets by a plastic tag ½-inch by 2­ inch in size, stamped with the cable run identification characters in ¼-inch letters and secured to the cable with two nylon tie-wrap devices. Each conductor shall have clear, distinctive and permanent bands for identification. These identification bands shall be used even though the conductors have clear markings within their insulation. Bands shall conform to the latest edition of Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction. These permanent identification bands shall be marked as specified. All conductors shall be labeled within each affected pull box. c. Interconnect 1) Direct Wire: Interconnect cable with 7 - #14 wires per LADOT Specification 92-039-03 (latest revision) shall be continuous from controller to controller, unless splices are specifically authorized by the LADOT Traffic Signal Inspector. Where splices are authorized by the LADOT Traffic Signal Inspector, they shall be soldered and shall be secured using vinyl, water-tight, spring tensioned, silicone filled, direct burial wire connectors, as described in LADOT Specification 56-002-03 (latest revision). 2) Multi-Pair Interconnect Cable: Filled telephone type cable shall consist of paired #22 AWG solid annealed copper conductors. The cable shall be polyethylene insulated and aluminum shielded, conforming to the construction requirements and environmental, mechanical, and electrical tests of LADOT Specification 92-069-01 (latest revision) for filled telephone cable. The cable sizes shall be 6, 12, 25, 50, and 75 pair. Cable splices shall only be made at a communication cabinet, splice vault or controller. Punch down the “IN” cable on the left side of the T-66 block and the “OUT” cable(s) on the right side of the T-66 block. 3) Telephone and Fire Alarm: Interconnect cable using telephone lines or former fire alarm lines shall be #14 AWG stranded twisted pair copper wire having 600-volt insulation and overall shield and jacket. d. Inductive Loops Detector Inductive loop detectors shall be installed as per LADOT Standard Drawing S-70.1A or as otherwise approved by LADOT. To the greatest extent practical, loops should be installed in one continuous medium. Loop wire shall conform to LADOT Specification 92-093-01 (latest revision). All detector lead-in cable connections and terminations shall be soldered. 1) Wire Splicing: Where circuits are to be spliced, each splice shall be twisted 12

clean.title: Bicycle Detector; Light Rail Train (LRT) Track Detector Loop
clean.summary: Two LADOT detector sheets. The first (S-70.1D) shows bicycle detector loops. Case I is a pair of 3 ft loops for bicycle only (bike lane) and Case II is a pair of 6 ft loops for bicycle and vehicle, with winding details and saw cut sections. The second (S-70.4A, sheet 3 of 3) shows the preformed 30 in LRT track detector loop and the Type A LRT detector handhole.

pages.text: and soldered with rosin core (no acid core or acid paste shall be used) then sealed with vinyl, watertight, spring tensioned, silicone filled, direct burial wire connector per LADOT Specification 56-002-03 (latest revision). 2) Loop Detector Wire Routing System: Unless otherwise specified, all detector loops shall be wound in a clockwise direction. The input (or start) wire shall be tagged with an odd number, the output (or finish) wire with the next higher number. A plastic tag ½-inch by 2-inch shall be tie wrapped around each loop pair to identify each pair by phase and numbers of individual conductors. 3) Sealant: The loop wires shall be covered and sealed using Caltrans approved “Hot-Melt Rubberized Asphalt Sealant” for loop installation. Note: “Hot-Melt Crack Sealant” shall not be used in place of the above. 4) Transit Bus or Photo Red-Light Detector Wire: All Transit Bus or Photo Red-Light loop wire shall conform to IMSA Specification 51-7. e. Conductor Splicing and Termination 1) Connectors All spliced solid field conductors shall be twisted together and secured using vinyl, water-tight, spring tensioned, silicone filled, direct burial wire connectors, as described in LADOT Specification 56-002-03 (latest revision). At least 36 inches of surplus signal cable shall be neatly coiled in a clockwise direction within each pull box. Of these 36 inches of cable, only 24 inches of outer jacket shall be removed. The remaining 12 inches of cable shall remain enclosed within the outer jacket for future emergency repair needs. Care shall be used in removing the outer cable jacket to ensure that the individual conductor insulation is not cut or nicked. Failure to protect the individual conductor insulation shall result in the replacement of the damaged cable at contractor’s expense. 2) Multi-Conductor Signal Cables in the Controller Pull Box The installation of new multi-conductor cable(s) into and through the controller pull box shall be spliced together as referenced in paragraph 1) and not looped through, except for: a) Service wires b) Communication cables c) Loop detector lead-in cables d) Railroad preemption cables or wires e) Telephone interconnect cables f) Video cables or conductors 3) All stranded wires shall be terminated with an LADOT approved terminal connector and properly compressed for minimum resistance at the attachment. 4) Where optimum operation of circuits requires minimum resistance, as determined by the LADOT Traffic Signal Inspector, the connections and 13

pages.title: 2) Ground: Each circuit shall be tested for grounds.
pages.text: terminals shall be soldered. f. Inductive Loop Detector Lead-in Cable All inductive loop detector lead-in cable from the pull box to the controller cabinet shall have two-, three- or four-pair conductors and shall conform to Standard Drawing S-70.2. and LADOT Specification 92-082-03 (latest revision). A maximum of 12” of outer jacket shall be removed. g. Transit Bus or Photo Red-Light Detector Lead-in Cable All Transit Bus or Photo Red-Light detector lead-in cable from the pull box to the controller cabinet shall be one pair cable and conform to IMSA Specification 50-2. h. Conductors Attached to Controller Field Terminals Each controller field terminal shall have a maximum of one wire connected. If the intersection wiring plan requires more than the single wire to accomplish the correct operation, splicing the conductors in the controller pull box shall be used. 1) Compression terminal connectors shall not be used when connecting solid wires to controller terminals. 2) Compression terminal connectors shall be used when connecting stranded wires to controller terminals, and shall be soldered. i. Field Testing Prior to start of functional testing, the Contractor shall perform the following tests on all circuits, in the presence of the DOT Inspector and/or Engineer. 1) Continuity: Each circuit shall be tested for continuity. When 120V AC is used to conduct a “dynamic, non-destructive” test of the circuit(s), then suitable circuit protection shall be used. Suitable circuit protection shall be in the form of a low amperage fuse or circuit breaker with a design curve that reacts fast enough to trip and protect the circuit under test without interrupting any of the cabinet circuit breakers. 2) Ground: Each circuit shall be tested for grounds. 3) Insulation Resistance: An insulation resistance test at 500 Volts DC shall be made on each circuit between the circuit and a ground. The insulation resistance shall not be less than 10 Megohms on all circuits, except for inductive loop detector circuits, which shall have an insulation resistance value of not less than 100 Megohms. 14

pages.title: 5. FIBER OPTIC CABLE
pages.text: 5. FIBER OPTIC CABLE a. General 1) Description: Fiber Optic Trunk Cable shall be of loose-tube construction. The optical fibers shall be single mode optical glass or as specified by the Engineer. The fiber optic cable shall conform to ICEA S-87-640. 2) Performance: The optical performance of each single-mode fiber measured at wave lengths of both 1310 nanometers and 1550 nanometers shall have maximum attenuation of 0.4 decibels per kilometer at 1310 nanometers and 0.3 decibels per kilometer at 1550 nanometers and shall conform to TIA/EIA 49Z C4AA. 3) Construction: The cable shall be constructed using five or six gel-filled, color-coded buffer tubes stranded (reverse oscillation) around a dielectric central member. The color-coded fibers shall be contained in the buffer tubes and the remaining fillers shall be natural or white in color. A layer of aramid yarn (e.g. Kevlar) shall hold the tubes in position around the central member and provide tensile strength. The color code for the fibers shall be blue, orange, green brown, slate and white. Water blocking shall be of the dry-tape type within the interstitial spaces, and gel within the buffer tubes. 4) Jacket: The filled cable core shall be covered with a black, medium density polyethylene jacket. This outer jacket shall be abrasion and crack resistant, non-nutrient to fungus, electronically non-conductive and compatible with all cable components to which it may come in contact. The jacket shall be free from holes, splits, blisters or other imperfections. 5) End Termination Cable: Shall be of the tight-buffered type and shall contain two single-mode fibers protected by a yellow jacket and aramid yarn (e.g. Kevlar) strength member. The length of a typical end termination cable shall not exceed 100 feet. Connectors for end termination cables shall be ST unless otherwise specified by the Engineer. 6) Identification: Each length of cable shall be permanently identified by specifying the manufacturer and type of cable at intervals not greater than six feet along the outside of the outer jacket. Each length of cable shall be permanently marked with foot (or meter) markings at intervals not greater than three feet (or one meter). 7) Reels: The cable shall be wound on standard reels in a manner which provides access to both ends of the cable for testing while the cable is still on the reel. 8) Installation: Cable installation and handling procedures shall be in accordance with accepted industry standards and/or manufacturer’s recommendations and shall be performed by adequately trained and certified personnel. In all type 3 pull boxes, there shall be 10 feet minimum of extra looped cable for each cable entering or leaving the box. 15

pages.title: 6. CONTROLLER
pages.text: b. Splicing of Fiber Optic Cable Splicing of the Fiber Optic Cable shall be done by the fusion technique. All cables shall be carefully prepared and spliced in accordance with the cable manufacturer’s recommendations. Either heat shrinkable tubing shall protect the finished splices, metal protective sleeves or by some other method approved by the Engineer. All splices must be tested and documented after encasement. No splice shall exceed a 0.05 decibel loss. The completed splices shall be enclosed in re-enterable splice enclosures that seal to form moisture resistant protection. The splice case or enclosure shall contain a removable splice organizer or crib that shall secure the individual fibers and protect the splices. The splice organizer shall be attached to the strength members in the fiber optic cable. There shall be adequate space inside the enclosure to hold at least three feet of buffer tubes from each cable. There shall be no splices except as authorized by the LADOT Traffic Signal Inspector. Splice enclosures shall be Corning 6C22-02 (or equivalent) unless otherwise authorized by the LADOT Traffic Signal Inspector. Fiber optic interconnect cables may only be spliced at special fiber optics splice boxes as shown on the plans. Video fiber optic cable shall be spliced in double-deep, type 3 pull boxes. 6. CONTROLLER The contractor-supplied controllers shall conform to the latest LADOT material specification and addendum for the Model 2070 controller assembly, with either Type 332 or 337 cabinet as shown on the traffic signal plan, and all auxiliary equipment required to provide a complete functioning controller per LADOT Specifications 054-053-07 (latest revision). 7. GROUND RODS Copper ground rods shall be installed in all controller foundations and all service pull boxes. For a post-top mounted controller cabinet on existing or new F-8 foundation, an 8-foot by ½- inch diameter ground rod shall be installed in the controller pull box. For a Type 332 cabinet on F-332 foundation, an 8-foot by ½-inch diameter ground rod shall be installed in the foundation. For a Type M communication cabinet on F-12A foundation, an 8-foot by ½-inch diameter ground rod shall be installed in the foundation. A green #8 AWG copper wire (solid or stranded) shall be connected from the cabinet "Equipment Ground Bus" bar to the ground rod in the foundation or in RARE CASES as approved by the LADOT Traffic Signal Inspector, the controller pull box. The connection device to the ground rod shall be appropriate for the copper wire used. 16

pages.title: 8. SERVICE
pages.text: 8. SERVICE a. Service conductors shall be continuous without splices from the service pull box to the controller service connection. b. A voltage measurement shall be made between the service hot and neutral terminals before the main circuit breaker in the controller assembly. If the voltage is less than 110 volts AC notify the LADOT traffic signal inspector. c. A resistance measurement shall be made between the service neutral terminal and the chassis ground terminal. If the resistance is more than 4.0 ohms notify the LADOT traffic signal inspector. 9. SIGNAL HEADS a. Vehicle and Pedestrian Signal Heads Covers Shall conform to LADOT Specification 92-086-03 (latest revision). b. Vehicle Heads 1) Each signal section housing shall conform to LADOT Specification 92-061­ 06 (latest revision) for Vehicle Signal Heads, 8-inch and 12-inch glass filled polycarbonate. 2) A minimum of two vehicle heads for each and every phase shall be in operation while work is being performed at the intersection. Non-functioning vehicle heads shall be covered or turned away from the intersection c. Pedestrian Heads 1) Each pedestrian signal housing shall conform to LADOT Specification 92­ 064-06 (latest revision) for Pedestrian Signal Heads, glass filled polycarbonate. 2) One visible operating pedestrian head shall be provided at all times for each direction of each signalized crosswalk while work is being performed at the intersection. Non-functioning pedestrian heads at a signalized crosswalk shall be covered or turned away from the intersection. d. Traffic Signal Visors – All vehicle signal indications shall be provided with removable visors per LADOT Specification 92-061-06 (latest revision). If beveled or long visors are specified on the traffic signal plans, they shall conform to Standard Drawings S-76.3, S-76.6 or S-76.7. e. Light Emitting Diode (LED) Signal Modules – All new traffic signal modules shall be LED, and shall conform to LADOT Specification 92-088-06 (latest revision). 17

Each refers to the ear detail on S-76.3 and to LADOT Purchase Specification #92-061-06.

pages.title: 10. DETECTORS
pages.text: 10. DETECTORS The contractor shall replace and restore operation of any damaged detectors (inductive loop, video or other type) within two (2) working days after the completion of construction on the portion of the roadway where the detectors were damaged. Devices other than those identified in the LADOT Specification 54-055-01 (latest revision), must be submitted for test, evaluation, and approval to the LADOT Traffic Signal Lab Research and Development Section, at least 90 days prior to expected date of activation. Contact the Signal Repair Section Supervisor at (213) 847-2943 for specifications applicable to the device being submitted. 11. LINES AND GRADES a) All new or relocated traffic signal work shall be located as per the design plans and engineering specifications. b) Any reference to curb line on the plans or in the engineering specifications shall be made once the permanent curb and gutter is installed, prior to excavating any new foundations that are called for on the plans. c) Contractor shall assume all responsibility for accuracy of foundation installation, including removal of foundations installed at unacceptable elevations and restoration of the soil prior to reinstallation of proposed foundation, at their own expense. 12. ANCHOR BOLT HEIGHT See Section 307-10.1 “Standards and Steel Pedestals” in the Standard Specification for Public Works Construction for anchor bolt height requirements. 18

Callouts: Pole; 3/4" base plate; T (Wall thickness) = 0.1196"; See Detail A; Detail B; 4.5" O.D. at top; 2 1/4" diameter hole (Drill 1 side only); Two 3/4" diameter holes (Drill through); 3" X 5" Hand hole reinforced with 1/4" X 2" ring welded to outside of pole and 1/8" cover plate; 0.50" NC square nut holder with fastener for grounding welded to interior of pole shaft at 180 degrees from hand hole rim; 1/4" plate with 2" central hole; Foundation see S-52.1.
clean.description:
Standards Type 1, 1A, 8, 8A and 9, drawing S-51.1.3A (sheet 1 of 1). The sheet combines several details and five pole elevations.

Base Plate (plan): a 10" square plate with rounded corners and four slotted anchor bolt holes near the corners. Dimensions: 10" sq., 9 1/2" bolt circle and 8 1/2" bolt circle (the slots span between these two circles), each slot 1 1/4" X 1 3/4" for anchor bolt, with 1 3/4" and 1 1/4" slot dimensions shown. The central circle is the pole.

Elevation A: a partial cutaway of the pole welded to a 3/4" base plate. Pole wall thickness T = 0.1196" (shown twice). Weld callouts: a 1/4" fillet at the top of the joint and a 1/8" fillet at the inside bottom. A circle marks the weld area, labeled See Detail A.

Detail A (enlarged weld section): pole wall (hatched) meets the base plate with a built-up weld. Dimensions: 1.83 T Min. (height up the wall), 1.57 T Min. (length along the plate), T (weld throat) and 30 degrees Max. contact angle.

Detail B (Pole Top Tenon): a short tube 4 1/2" O.D., 4 NPS Std, 4.00" tall, passing through a 1/4" plate with 2" central hole welded to the pole shaft with 3/16" welds at both faces (3/16 callouts), 1/4" Min. Typ. weld size noted at the left. Labeled Pole shaft below.

Pole elevations: TYPE 1 (tall left pole in the center group): overall 10'-6" from the top of the base plate to the top, 4.06" O.D. at top, 5.48" O.D. at base. Holes: a 2 1/4" diameter hole (drill 1 side only) and two 3/4" diameter holes (drill through) located 4.5" above and 4.5" below the center of the large hole, with 2'-11.5" from the top to the upper hole. A 3" X 5" hand hole reinforced with 1/4" X 2" ring welded to outside of pole and 1/8" cover plate is at the base (see Elevation A). TYPE 1A: overall 14'-0", 3.57" O.D. at top, 5.48" O.D. at base, same hole pattern (2 1/4" hole with two 3/4" holes 4.5" above and below) with 6'-5.5" from the top to the upper hole. A 0.50" NC square nut holder with fastener for grounding is welded to the interior of the pole shaft at 180 degrees from the hand hole rim. TYPE 8: 1'-8" tall, 4.5" O.D. at top, 4.73" O.D. at base. TYPE 8A: 2'-4" tall, 4.5" O.D. at top, 4.83" O.D. at base. TYPE 9: 7'-2" tall, 4.29" O.D. at top, 5.25" O.D. at base. Each shaft has a Detail B tenon at the top.

Foundation section (Type 1): concrete foundation with anchor bolts, labeled Foundation see S-52.1, 24" X 24" plan (24" diameter optional) and 3'-6" deep, set beside a stepped curb and sidewalk. Elbowed conduit not dimensioned.

clean.summary: LADOT drawing S-51.9.5 for the Type 16 signal mast arm pole, an 18 ft tapered steel pole with a 15 to 20 ft arm and one signal head. It gives the arm connection plate details, 11 1/2 inch square base plate, pole and arm schedules, a Type F-2 foundation 32 by 32 inches, and fabrication notes.
clean.notes:
Notes (circled):
(1) Round tapered steel tube with maximum taper of .15 inches per foot. End section O.D. of 2 3/8" for mounting hardware. Standard 2" pipe extensions of 3'-0" max. length may be used at the option of the manufacturer.
(2) 4 anchor bolts each base plate. Length indicated does not include required 4"-90 degree bend. Each anchor bolt is threaded 6" at the top and is furnished with 2 nuts & 2 washers. One anchor bolt bonded to conduit.
1. Pole and signal arm shall be fabricated from sheet steel conforming to the specifications of ASTM Designation A611 Grade C, or ASTM Designation A 570 Grade C.
2. All welding shall conform to AWS D2.0 "Specifications for welded Highway and Railway Bridges."
3. All structural steel shall conform to ASTM designation A36, except as otherwise shown.
Notes (second list):
1. Alternative details approved by the Engineer may be subst. for the arm connections and configurations shown.
2. Fabricators electing to use larger than min. arm diameters must adjust the details as required to permit solid seating of cap screws.
3. In lieu of the torque requirements for HS bolts, cap screws shall be tightened by the turn-of-nut method 1/6 turn from snug tight condition. No washer will be required.
4. Only one signal head may be mounted on each signal arm.
5. All metal parts shall be galvanized after fabrication.
6. All arms shall be bent to the approximate configuration shown.

It shows hole details, an 11 1/2 inch square base plate, a Type F-2 foundation with four 1 1/8 inch by 40 inch anchor bolts, and mounting heights of 22.3 or 23.3 ft by arm length.

Note: Standard must conform to Bureau of Street Lighting Plan L-103-0.
Callouts: Mast Arm; 3/4" Drill Thru, 2 Holes; 2 1/4" Drill, One side; Detail - Side Opposite Mast Arm; Pole Base Plate; Street Grade; Top of Curb; Tapered steel pole; Foundation, Type F-2; Anchor Bolts 1 1/8" X 40" X 4" (4 required).

clean.description:
CD954 Standard, drawing S-51.9.6. One elevation with details.

Elevation: a 30'-0" tapered steel pole (overall height to pole top) with a curved mast arm extending to the left and a luminaire arm with a cobra head luminaire extending to the left near the top. The mast arm is labeled Mast Arm, and its horizontal length is 15'-0" (Unless otherwise specified), measured from the end of the arm to the pole. A three lens signal head is drawn dashed at the arm end. Left vertical dimensions: Mounting Height (to the arm), 17'-6" Min. (to the bottom of the signal head). Right of the pole: 30'-0" overall, 17'-6" to the mast arm connection, 17'-6" (to the signal head lower edge), 11'-3" and 7'-6" to dashed pedestrian equipment mounted on the pole, all measured from street grade. A dash dotted leader from the pole points to the Detail - Side Opposite Mast Arm.

Detail - Side Opposite Mast Arm: pole cross shaft showing the hole pattern 3/4" Drill Thru, 2 Holes and 2 1/4" Drill, One side, with spacing 9" overall and 4 1/2" between holes.

Pole Base Plate: 11 1/2" Square plate with R=1 1/2" corners, 11 1/2" Bolt Circle, a central cutout with four slots on the diagonals, Axis of Arms marked, slot width dimensions 3/4" and 1 1/2".

Foundation section: Tapered steel pole on Foundation, Type F-2 with Anchor Bolts 1 1/8" X 40" X 4" (4 required). The foundation is set beside a stepped curb with Street Grade and Top of Curb marked, 36" from the pole to the curb, 14" Min. from the top surface to the conduit.

Table: Mast Arm Length and Mounting Height. 15', 22.3' +/- . 18', 23.3' +/- . (revision 1) 20', 23.3' +/- .

clean.description:
100 MPH Poles, sheet 1 of 2, drawing S-52.1.6. The sheet shows a foundation elevation, Section A-A, a base plate plan and a schedule table.

Foundation elevation: a pole shaft sits on a base plate with anchor bolts in a cast-in-drilled-hole concrete pile. Type 560-C-3250 concrete with a Reinforcing cage near the bottom. Dimensions: 36" from the curb to the pole centerline, 18" min. depth to the conduit, Depth (pile depth, from the schedule), 3" clearance below the cage, and Diameter (pile diameter, from the schedule). Anchor bolts (2 nuts & 2 washers required per bolt), total 4, are threaded 8" at the top and galvanized 12", with 1" +/- 1/4" and 2" Min. to 3" Max. mortar under the plate. After plumbing standard, place mortar all around bolts. Finish with slope ranging from 45 to 90 degrees including drain holes. Finished grade is marked. Callouts: #8 Green bonding wire; 4" X 6 1/2" Hand Hole reinforced with ring welded to outside of pole, see note 2, 1/8" cover plate, 8" dimension to the plate; 0.50" NC square nut holder with fastener for grounding welded to interior of pole shaft at 180 degrees from hand hole rim; Traffic signal conduit (2"); Street lighting conduit (1"). Section cut A-A is marked on the pile.

Section A-A, Cast-in-drilled-hole (CIDH) pile foundation: a circular section with Diameter dimension, 2" clearance to the cage, #8 - total 10 longitudinal bars, and #4 @ 6" or #4 spiral @ 6" pitch with 1'-6" lap @ splice and 135 degree hook @ terminations. Centerlines marked.

Base plate: a square plate with side C, bolt circle, four anchor bolt slots on the diagonals, 3" and 2 3/8" (2 5/8" for 60 - 5 - 100 & 61 - 5 - 100) dimensions and a 1 1/2" dimension.

Table of 100 MPH poles (12 types). Columns: TYPE, Standard Height, Mast Arm Length, F Min. Spacing, CIDH Pile Foundation (Dia., Depth, Cage Dia., Cage Depth), Anchor Bolts, Bolt Circle, C. clean.title: 100 MPH Poles (Sheet 2 of 2): Side Mount Indications Drill Detail
clean.summary: Shows how a 100 mph signal pole is drilled for side-mounted signal indications and tagged. A three-hole pattern on the side opposite the mast arm uses two 3/4 in. through holes and one 2 1/4 in. hole, spaced 4 1/2 in. and 9 in. Side-mounted indications sit at 7'-6" and 11'-3" above grade. Metal tags give the pole type, load case, design wind velocity, mast arm length and height.
clean.notes:
1. Title of detail: Side Mount Indications Drill Detail.
2. Mast arm length is measured from the pole to the outermost signal head. Signal head spacings are labeled F1 and F2, values not given on this sheet.
3. Side view opposite of mast arm: two 3/4 in. diameter holes (drill through) and one 2 1/4 in. diameter hole (drill 1 side only), spaced 4 1/2 in. and 9 in. as shown.
4. Metal tag on mast arm: LA-XX-X-XXX-XX, reading type, load case, design wind velocity, actual mast arm length (feet (FT)).
5. Metal tag at hand hole: LA-XX-X-XXX-XX-XX, reading type, load case, design wind velocity, maximum (MAX.) mast arm length (FT), height (FT).
6. Side-mounted indications are at 7'-6" and 11'-3" above grade.
7. Cast-in-drilled-hole (CIDH) foundation: see detail on sheet 1.
clean.description:
Elevation of a 100 mph signal pole with a mast arm, drawn with the arm projecting to the left of a vertical pole. A luminaire arm curves up and to the left from the pole top. The mast arm lies below it and carries three vertical three-section signal heads, drawn as rounded rectangles with three circles each. A horizontal dimension labeled Mast Arm Length runs from the outermost signal head to the pole centerline. Along the arm, F1 is the spacing between the first and second heads and F2 is the spacing between the second and third heads, with no numeric values given. A fourth, separate four-section signal head is drawn below the first head on a short stub of arm that is cut off with a break mark at the second head position, showing a four-section head option. A vertical dimension labeled Standard Height runs from grade to the top of the pole.

Metal tag on the mast arm: a rectangular tag reading LA-XX-X-XXX-XX, with a curved leader to the underside of the mast arm near the pole. Its fields are labeled TYPE, LOAD CASE, DESIGN WIND VELOCITY and ACTUAL MAST ARM LENGTH (FT).

Side-mounted indications on the pole: a three-section signal head and a pedestrian-style square indication are mounted on the side of the pole shaft below the mast arm, on the side opposite the mast arm. Two dash-dot reference lines from these heads lead across to the drill detail. Vertical dimensions from grade to the heads read 7'-6" (to the lower, square indication) and 11'-3" (to the upper three-section head). The Standard Height dimension line is the tallest one at the right.

Side view opposite of mast arm: an enlarged view of the pole shaft seen from the side opposite the mast arm, showing a vertical column of three holes on the pole centerline. Two small holes are called out as two 3/4 in. diameter holes (drill through) and one center hole is called out as a 2 1/4 in. diameter hole (drill 1 side only). The two small holes sit above and below the center hole. The dimension from the upper small hole to the center hole is 4 1/2 in., and the overall spacing between the two small holes is 9 in. The dash-dot lines from the signal head positions lead to this view.

Hand hole and metal tag at the base: a Hand Hole is shown on the pole shaft low on the pole with a curved leader. A second metal tag reading LA-XX-X-XXX-XX-XX is shown, with fields TYPE, LOAD CASE, DESIGN WIND VELOCITY, MAX. MAST ARM LENGTH (FT) and HEIGHT (FT). A curved leader runs from this tag to the hand hole.

Foundation: the pole stands on a base plate at grade over a rectangular cast-in-drilled-hole foundation drawn below the grade line, labeled CIDH Foundation, See Detail on Sheet 1.

clean.title: Camera Poles (Case 4 Mast Arm Loading - 100 MPH Wind Speed), Sheet 1 of 2
clean.summary: Sheet 1 of 2 of drawing S-52.1.4B for 45 foot CCTV camera poles, Types C-1-100 and C-2-100, with top-mount or side-mount camera options, optional signal heads, a 15 ft max. luminaire arm and a handhole. Type C-2-100 also carries a 45 ft max. signal arm with a street name sign. Gives pole dimensions, wall thickness, steel and finish specifications and general notes.
clean.notes:
Pole specifications:
Base plate and flanges: ASTM A-36.
Shaft: steel of 48,000 PSI minimum yield after fabrication. Design yield of Fy = 48,000 PSI in order that Fu/Fy > 1.5.
Pipe: ASTM A-53 Grade B.
Anchor bolts: ASTM A-307.
Welds: all butt welds to be ground flush with base metal.
Longitudinal: butt weld by the submerged arc process.
Circumferential: butt weld with permanent back-up ring.
Finish pole: hot-dip galvanized per ASTM A-123.
Finish hardware: hot-dip galvanized per ASTM A-153.

General notes:
1. Fabrication of the standards, luminaire arms and mast arms must conform to the 2006 Department of Transportation, State of California Standard Plans.
2. Refer to LADOT Standard Drawing No. S-52.1.6 for "F" spacing.
3. Projected luminaire arm length to be determined by Department of Public Works, Bureau of Street Lighting. Refer to Caltrans Standard Drawing No. ES-7C for luminaire arm connection detail.
4. Signal arm connection shall be for 45 ft. arm (Case 4 arm loading), as per Caltrans Standard Drawing No. ES-7F. Shorter arms may be used, as appropriate.
clean.description:
Elevation views: two pole elevations side by side, Type C-1-100 Pole at left and Type C-2-100 Pole at right. Both are 45 foot tapered steel poles for CCTV cameras, standing on a CIDH foundation drawn below a hatched grade line, with the foundation labeled See Foundation Detail, Sheet 2.

Type C-1-100 pole: pole height is 45'-0" with 12.125" base outside diameter (O.D.), 5.938" top O.D. and 0.4184" wall thickness (THK.). At the pole top, a Top-Mount Option (see Pan and Tilt Mounting Flange Detail, sheet 2) is shown, together with a Side-Mount Option (see Clamp and Side Mounted Camera Arm Detail, sheet 2), which is a horizontal camera arm 12' max. long projecting from the top of the pole. An Upper Handhole and Coupling is called out near the top (see detail, sheet 2). A luminaire arm 15' max. projects from the pole near 29'-6" above grade, with the callout See Note 3. Optional heads (signal heads) are shown on the lower pole, with a handhole near the base. Vertical dimensions from grade: 7'-6", 11'-3", 29'-6" and 45'-0".

Type C-2-100 pole: same 45'-0" pole with 12.125" base O.D. and 5.938" top O.D., with 0.6250" wall thickness. It has the same top-mount and side-mount camera options, upper handhole and coupling, and 15' max. luminaire arm (See Note 3). In addition it has a signal mast arm 45' max. long projecting to the left from the pole at about 16'-0" above grade (See Note 4). Two signal heads are on the arm separated by a sign, with spacing F between the heads ("F" spacing, see Note 2). A street name sign hangs from the arm, called out as Street Name Sign, See S-486.0. Optional heads and a handhole are on the lower pole. Vertical dimensions from grade: 7'-6", 11'-3", 16'-0", 29'-6" and 45'-0".

Pole specifications: a list under the C-1 pole, given in the notes field.

clean.title: Camera Poles (Case 4 Mast Arm Loading - 100 MPH Wind Speed), Sheet 2 of 2
clean.summary: Sheet 2 of 2 of drawing S-52.1.4B gives the camera pole details: pan and tilt mounting flange, upper handhole and coupling, clamp and side mounted camera arm, 18 in. base plate and the 36 in. by 10 ft CIDH foundation. The foundation carries a 32 in. reinforcing cage and three conduits. Design criteria and three foundation notes are included.
clean.notes:
Pan and tilt mounting flange detail: 4 - 3/8 in. diameter stainless steel studs, equally spaced on 4 3/4 in. diameter B.C. 6 1/2 in. diameter (ASTM A-36). 4 NF threads, stainless nuts and bolts. 1/2 in. plate. 1 1/4 in. 1/4 in. fillet weld.

Upper handhole and coupling detail: 2 in. coupling. 18 in. from pole top. Cable hook* welded to inside of shaft oriented directly opposite coupling and above handhole. 3 in. x 5 in. handhole rim (1/4 in. plate x 2 in. wide) and cover. 1/4 in. welds.
* Each cable shall be supported inside the pole by Kellems grips (or equivalent) one at the top and a second at the mid-point. Two 1/8 in. diameter galvanized steel wires shall secure mid-point grips to the top cable hook.

Clamp and side mounted camera arm detail: 3 in. Schedule 40 pipe (hot-dip galvanized per ASTM A-153). 1/2 in. U bolt ASTM A-307. 3/8 in. plate clamp. 6-1/2 in. diameter x 1/2 in. thick plate (ASTM A-36). 12' max. 4 - 3/8 in. diameter stainless steel studs, equally spaced on 4 3/4 in. diameter B.C. 1/2 in. plate. 1/4 in. gusset plate each side. 1/4 in. welds, 2 places.

Base plate detail: 18 in. x 18 in. Hole diameter = pole inside diameter - 2 in. 4 holes, equally spaced on 18 in. diameter B.C. Diagonal offset dimensions 3 in., 1 1/2 in., 2 3/8 in.

Foundation detail: finished grade. Base plate 18 in. x 18 in. x 1.75 in. 4 in. topping. 4 1/2 in. (4)2 in. x 42 in. x 6 in. anchor bolts with 2 nuts and 2 washers per bolt (one above and one below the plate). Bonding strap or wire. 12 2/5 in. 3 in. conduit (traffic). 1 in. conduit (BSL). 2 in. conduit (CCTV cable). Foundation 36 in. wide, 10' deep. Reinforcing cage: 32 in. cage diameter, 9'-6" cage depth, see detail of Section A-A in LADOT Std. Dwg No. S-52.1.6.

Foundation design criteria: wind load design based on 2001 AASHTO Standard Specifications for Structural Support for Highway Signs, Luminaires, and Traffic Signals. (Fatigue requirements of Chapter 11 are not considered.) Wind speed = 100 mph.

Notes:
1. Bar reinforcement shall conform to ASTM A615 Grade 60.
2. All soils supporting and surrounding the foundation shall be undisturbed natural soil or 90% compacted fill.
3. Foundation concrete shall be 560-C-3250.
clean.description:
Pan and tilt mounting flange detail: a plan and an elevation of the top-mount camera flange. The plan shows a 6 1/2 in. diameter (ASTM A-36) round plate with 4 stainless steel studs, 3/8 in. diameter, equally spaced on a 4 3/4 in. diameter bolt circle (B.C.). The elevation shows a 1/2 in. plate welded to the pipe top with a 1/4 in. fillet weld, 4 NF threads with stainless nuts and bolts, and studs projecting 1 1/4 in. above the plate.

Upper handhole and coupling detail: a section through the pole shaft near the top. A 2 in. coupling is welded on one side with a 1/4 in. weld, and a 3 in. x 5 in. handhole rim (1/4 in. plate x 2 in. wide) and cover is welded on the opposite side with 1/4 in. welds. The coupling and handhole are located 18 in. from the pole top. A cable hook, welded to the inside of the shaft, is oriented directly opposite the coupling and above the handhole. A footnote marked with an asterisk explains cable support.

Clamp and side mounted camera arm detail: a plan and elevation of the side-mount arm. A 3 in. Schedule 40 pipe (hot-dip galvanized per ASTM A-153) runs up to 12' max. between a clamp on the pole and a 6 1/2 in. diameter x 1/2 in. thick plate (ASTM A-36) at the camera end. The clamp consists of a 1/2 in. U bolt (ASTM A-307) and a 3/8 in. plate clamp, with 1/4 in. fillet welds. The end plate has 4 stainless steel studs, 3/8 in. diameter, equally spaced on a 4 3/4 in. diameter B.C. In elevation the pipe end plate is a 1/2 in. plate with 1/4 in. gusset plates on each side and 1/4 in. welds, 2 places.

Base plate detail: plan of an 18 in. x 18 in. square base plate with rounded corners, a center hole with diameter equal to the pole inside diameter minus 2 in., and 4 holes equally spaced on an 18 in. diameter bolt circle at the corners. Diagonal offset dimensions of 3 in., 1 1/2 in. and 2 3/8 in. are given for the bolt hole pattern.

Foundation detail: section through the CIDH foundation, 36 in. wide and 10' deep. A base plate 18 in. x 18 in. x 1.75 in. sits at finished grade on a 4 in. topping, with a 4 1/2 in. dimension at the top. Four anchor bolts, 2 in. x 42 in. x 6 in., each with 2 nuts and 2 washers (one above and one below the plate), are cast in. A bonding strap or wire is shown under the plate. The dimension between conduits is 12 2/5 in. Three conduits enter the foundation: 3 in. conduit (traffic), 1 in. conduit (BSL) and 2 in. conduit (CCTV cable). A reinforcing cage is drawn in the lower part of the foundation, 32 in. cage diameter and 9'-6" cage depth, see detail of Section A-A in LADOT Std. Dwg No. S-52.1.6.

clean.summary: Typical installation of Bureau of Street Lighting poles carrying a rectangular rapid flashing beacon sign arm, drawing S-52.1.7. Shows the single luminaire arm poles CD953A, B and C and the twin-arm poles CD953-A2, B2 and C2, each with an 8 ft max. sign arm, W11-2 signs, RRFBs, a control cabinet, solar panel and pushbutton. Foundation details are on sheet 4.
clean.notes:
1. Tilt solar panel to 60 degrees and rotate assembly so collector panel will face due south.
2. Arm projection 8' max. from the pole.
3. Signs and devices: W11-2(2), RRFB's (back to back), W16-7p(2), pedestrian pushbutton, control cabinet. Detail B (back to back), Detail D.
4. Dimensions: 17' min. above grade to the bottom of the upper RRFB assembly, 42 in. and 84 in. heights above grade at the pushbutton and W16-7p(2) levels, 36 in. from the pole centerline to the pad edge.

clean.description:
Typical installation elevations, not to scale, of two BSL (Bureau of Street Lighting) poles with a Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon (RRFB) sign arm. The left pole is BSL Poles (CD953A, CD953B, CD953C) and the right pole is BSL Poles (CD953-A2, CD953-B2, CD953-C2). Both are drawn identically except the left pole has a single luminaire arm curving to the left and the right pole has two luminaire arms curving left and right.

Upper pole: a pole-top finial sits above a luminaire arm. A solar panel is mounted on a short arm on the pole with the note Tilt solar panel to 60 deg and rotate assembly so collector panel will face due south. Two horizontal arms project to the left, each at most 8' max. from the pole, attached to the pole by clamps called out as Detail D. The arms carry a W11-2 pedestrian crossing sign, shown as a diamond with walking figure, mounted between them, with RRFB lights below the sign, called out as Detail B (Back to Back). The bottom of the RRFB assembly is at 17' min. above grade, shown by a vertical dimension with a break symbol.

Lower pole: below a break, a Control Cabinet is mounted on the pole. Below it is a W11-2(2) pedestrian crossing sign, with RRFB's (Back to Back) below it, and a W16-7p(2) supplemental arrow plaque below the RRFBs. A Pedestrian Pushbutton is mounted on the pole, with dimensions of 42 in. from grade to the pushbutton level and 84 in. from grade to the bottom of the W16-7p(2) plaque level. The pole base has a base plate on a concrete foundation with a sidewalk or pad stepped to the left, with a 36 in. dimension from the pole centerline to the edge of the pad. Callout: Foundation Details, See Sheet 4.

A 45 degree angle is shown at each of two radial lines on the right side. Conduit stubs project radially from the footing at the right and bottom, with a conduit cluster at the center.

Section view (bottom): a section through the foundation and sidewalk topping. The footing is 36 in. wide and 60 in. deep. A topping at least 4 in. thick sits on top of the footing, with the sidewalk or pad stepped to the left and 36 in. from the pole centerline to the pad edge. A bushing sits 2 3/4 in. above the topping. A bonding strap or wire is shown at the pole. Reinforcement is (8) #10 long reinforced bars with #4 ties at 9 in. on center (OC), typical (TYP.), provide (2) ties at 2 in. OC at top. Clearances of 3 in. and 2 in. are called out at the left side and 3 in. clear at the bottom. Anchor bolts are 1 1/8 in. x 40 in. x 4 in., 2 nuts and 2 washers per bolt, ASTM F1554 Grade 55 bolts. A 1 in. diameter street light conduit and a 2 in. diameter traffic signal conduit enter the footing, the traffic signal conduit stubbing out 6 in. min. beyond the footing face. A 14 in. min. dimension is shown on the right side at the upper part of the footing.

clean.title: Temporary Signal for Type 1 Standard
clean.summary: Drawing S-57.2B shows a temporary signal on a Type 1 standard held by a 36 in. square steel platform and four 5 gallon concrete-filled cans chained around the pole. It gives the platform plan and underside layout, bolt circle, lip, notches and a weight block detail of at least 90 lbs. It requires leveling on slopes steeper than 1/2 in. per foot.
clean.notes:
1. Use 12 in. heads corresponding to permanent heads being replaced.
2. 36 in. square (SQ.) x 1/4 in. thick (THK.) steel platform, hot dip galvanized per ASTM 123.
3. Type 1 base with 4 1 in. diameter x 3-1/2 in. bolts and nuts with 2 washers for each bolt.
4. 3/8 in. diameter steel coil chain tied to each 5 gal. block and locked around the Type 1 standard.
5. 5 gal. can filled with concrete. Four cans are required, spaced as shown.
6. 2 in. high x 1/4 in. thick perimeter lip resting on ground.
7. 1-3/4 in. x 1-3/4 in. x 1/4 in. steel angle brackets welded to plate.
8. 4 holes at 1-1/4 in. diameter. 8-1/2 in. diameter bolt circle.
9. 1 in. x 1 in. notches for cable.
10. For slopes greater than 1/2 in. rise per foot, temporary standard to be set level through the use of grading or wood shims.
11. Weight block: 5 gal. can filled with concrete, minimum weight 90 lbs. 1/2 in. diameter steel rod embedded 9 in. deep. 'LADOT' or contractor name embossed or welded on at least two sides.
clean.description:
Platform, top view detail (not to scale): a 36 in. x 36 in. square steel platform in plan. Four circles mark the four 5 gallon cans filled with concrete, one near each corner. A Type 1 base sits at the center of the platform with 4 bolts, and a 3/8 in. diameter steel coil chain is run through each can and locked around the Type 1 standard.

Platform, bottom view detail (not to scale): 36 in. x 36 in. in plan, with steel angle brackets crossing the underside as a framed grid. 4 holes at 1-1/4 in. diameter are laid out on an 8-1/2 in. diameter bolt circle at the center. 1 in. x 1 in. notches for cable are cut at the perimeter lip near the lower right corner.

Elevation: a temporary signal on a Type 1 standard. A signal head with three 12 in. sections, a second three-section head on a mast arm, a street name sign, and a pedestrian signal head (hand and walking person) are mounted on the pole. At the bottom, two 5 gal. concrete blocks sit on the platform and are chained around the Type 1 standard. The base assembly is bolted to the platform, which has a 2 in. high lip. Callouts: 1 in. x 1 in. notch for cable, LADOT name on the platform. A note beside the plate says for slopes greater than 1/2 in. rise per foot, the temporary standard is to be set level through the use of grading or wood shims.

Weight block (not to scale): a 5 gal. can filled with concrete, 12 in. wide by 14 in. tall, with a 1/2 in. diameter steel rod loop at the top embedded 9 in. deep, the loop 4 in. wide and projecting 3 in. above the can. Minimum weight is 90 lbs. LADOT or contractor name is embossed or welded on at least two sides.

clean.title: Signal, Temporary for Type CD954 Standard (Without Luminaire Arm)
clean.summary: Drawing S-57.2C shows a temporary traffic signal on a Type CD954 standard without a luminaire arm. It sits on a 60 in. steel plate with eight precast concrete blocks, 3/8 in. cable loops and a 3/8 in. coil chain, with a mast arm up to 15 ft long and 17 ft 6 in. min. head clearance. Plan, elevation and Section A-A are given with three notes.
clean.notes:
1. The CD954 standard (without luminaire arm) shall conform to Dept. of Transportation, City of Los Angeles, standard dwg. # S-51.9.6 (foundation excluded).
2. The mast arm length shall not exceed 15'-0".
3. There shall be a maximum of 2 - 5 section signal heads and 2 - ped. heads mounted to the shaft and one 5-section signal head mounted at the end of mast arm.
Callouts: Tie with 3/8 in. coil chain. 60 in. x 60 in. Weld angles to plate, 5 in. x 3 in. x 1/2 in. typical (revision 1). 23 in. x 23 in. x 30 in. precast conc. block (4 req.). 23 in. x 13 in. x 30 in. precast conc. block (4 req.). 2 in. hole. Drill holes (4 req.) to accommodate 1-1/8 in. bolt size and 11-1/2 in. bolt circle. 3/8 in. cable, embed 12 in. deep (8 req.). Type CD954 std. (revision 2). 1-1/8 in. x 4 in. hex. hd. bolt, hex. nut, flat washer (4 req.). Weld bolts and 4 in. x 4 in. x 1/4 in. plate washer to 3/4 in. plate (revision 1). Mortar leveling bed, wedge edges until mortar sets. (Mortar is not required on C.A.B., dirt or when slope is less than 1/4 in. per ft.) 60 in. x 60 in. x 3/4 in. steel plate. Coat plate assembly with primer and traffic signal yellow paint (revision 1). Temporary O.H. signal wires (maximum span 100 feet). All 12 in. sections. 15'-0" max. 17'-6" min. 2 signal heads. Street name sign. 2 pedestrian heads. See plan and Section A-A. Roadway. Type CD 954 Std. (without luminaire arm) (revision 2).
clean.description:
Plan view: a 60 in. x 60 in. square footing assembly seen from above, made of precast concrete blocks laid in a 3 x 3 grid around the pole. Four 23 in. x 23 in. x 30 in. precast concrete blocks (4 req.) sit at the corners and four 23 in. x 13 in. x 30 in. precast concrete blocks (4 req.) sit at the middle of each side, with the pole in the center square. A 6 in. dimension is shown at the edge of the center block and a 6 in. dimension at the side. Steel angles 5 in. x 3 in. x 1/2 in. (typical) are shown at the corners and side midpoints, called out as weld angles to plate (revision 1 mark). A dashed square marks a 3/8 in. coil chain that ties the blocks together. A 2 in. hole is called out at the pole center. Four holes are drilled to accommodate a 1-1/8 in. bolt size on an 11-1/2 in. bolt circle. Section marks A and A are shown on the left and right of the plan.

Elevation: a Type CD954 standard (without luminaire arm) on a temporary base at the roadway. A mast arm up to 15'-0" max. long reaches left from the pole and carries one all-12 in. section signal head at its end. The signal head has three circles with two arrows in the lower rows. Temporary overhead (O.H.) signal wires with a maximum span of 100 feet are looped at the pole top. A vertical dimension of 17'-6" min. runs from the roadway to the bottom of the mast arm head. On the pole are 2 signal heads, each with five 12 in. sections (three round, two arrow), a street name sign, and 2 pedestrian heads. A callout reads See Plan and Section A-A, pointing at the base plate.

Section A-A: a vertical cut through the base. A 60 in. x 60 in. x 3/4 in. steel plate sits on an A.C. or P.C.C. surface over a mortar leveling bed. Blocks stand 30 in. high on the plate, each with a 3/8 in. cable embedded 12 in. deep forming a loop 4 in. above the block (8 req.). The pole is bolted to the plate with 1-1/8 in. x 4 in. hex. head bolts, hex. nuts and flat washers (4 req.), and 4 in. x 4 in. x 1/4 in. plate washers (4 req.). A 1/4 in. weld is shown typical. A level indicator is shown on the plate.

clean.title: Signal, Temporary for Type CD954 Standard (With Luminaire Arm)
clean.summary: Drawing S-57.2D shows a temporary signal on a Type CD954 standard with a 4 ft luminaire arm and a mast arm up to 15 ft long. The base is a 60 in. x 60 in. x 3/4 in. steel plate with eight precast concrete blocks, cable loops and a coil chain. Plan, elevation, Section A-A and three notes are given, with 17 ft 6 in. min. head clearance.
clean.notes:
1. The CD954 standard shall conform to Dept. of Transportation, City of Los Angeles, standard drawing # S-51.9.6 (foundation excluded).
2. The mast arm length shall not exceed 15'-0".
3. There shall be a maximum of 2 - 5 section signal heads and 2 - ped. heads mounted to the shaft and one 3-section signal head mounted at the end of mast arm. All signal heads to be polycarbonate type.
Callouts: Tie with 3/8 in. coil chain. Weld angles to plate 5 in. x 3 in. x 1/2 in. typical. 23 in. x 23 in. x 30 in. precast concrete block (4 req.). 23 in. x 13 in. x 30 in. precast concrete block (4 req.). 2 in. hole. 4 in. x 4 in. x 1/2 in. plate washer (4 req.). Drill 1-1/2 in. diameter holes (4 req.) for 1-1/8 in. bolt size and 11-1/2 in. bolt circle. 3/8 in. cable, embed 12 in. deep (8 req.). Type CD954 std. 1-1/8 in. x 4 in. hex. hd. bolt, hex. nut, flat washer (4 req.). Weld bolts and 4 in. x 4 in. x 1/2 in. plate washers to 3/4 in. plate. Mortar leveling bed, wedge edges until mortar sets. (Mortar is not required on C.A.B., dirt or when slope is less than 1/4 in. per foot.) 60 in. x 60 in. x 3/4 in. steel plate. Coat plate assembly with primer and traffic signal yellow paint. Temporary O.H. signal cable (maximum span 100 feet). 4'-0" luminaire arm. 15'-0" max. All 12 in. sections. 17'-6" min. Signal heads see note 3. Street name sign. 2 pedestrian heads. See plan and Section A-A. Roadway. Type CD 954 Std.
clean.description:
Plan view: a 60 in. x 60 in. square footing assembly seen from above, made of precast concrete blocks laid in a 3 x 3 grid around the pole. Four 23 in. x 23 in. x 30 in. precast concrete blocks (4 req.) are at the corners and four 23 in. x 13 in. x 30 in. precast concrete blocks (4 req.) are at the middle of each side. 5 in. x 3 in. x 1/2 in. steel angles are welded to the plate at the corners and side midpoints (typical). A dashed square marks the 3/8 in. coil chain tie. Called out at the pole center: a 2 in. hole, and 4 in. x 4 in. x 1/2 in. plate washers (4 req.). Four 1-1/2 in. diameter holes are drilled for the 1-1/8 in. bolt size on an 11-1/2 in. bolt circle. Dimensions of 6 in. are shown at the center block and side. Section marks A and A are on both sides.

Elevation: a Type CD954 standard with a 4'-0" luminaire arm at the top and a mast arm 15'-0" max. long carrying one all-12 in. section signal head. Temporary overhead (O.H.) signal cable (maximum span 100 feet) is looped at the pole top. A vertical dimension of 17'-6" min. runs from the roadway to the mast arm head. Signal heads (see Note 3), 12 in. sections, are on the shaft, with a street name sign and 2 pedestrian heads below. A callout reads See Plan and Section A-A. A hatched roadway line is shown at grade.

Section A-A: a vertical cut through the base. A 60 in. x 60 in. x 3/4 in. steel plate sits on A.C. or P.C.C. surface on a mortar leveling bed, with a 1/4 in. weld typical. Blocks stand 30 in. high with 3/8 in. cable embedded 12 in. deep, forming loops 4 in. high (8 req.). The pole is bolted with 1-1/8 in. x 4 in. hex. hd. bolt, hex. nut, flat washer (4 req.) and 4 in. x 4 in. x 1/2 in. plate washers (4 req.). A level indicator is shown on the plate.

clean.title: Temporary Controller for Type 8 Standard
clean.summary: Drawing S-57.3 shows a 337 controller cabinet mounted on a Type 8 standard for temporary use, held down by a 36 in. square steel platform and four 5 gallon concrete-filled cans chained around the pole. It gives the platform plan and underside layouts, bolt circle, lip and notches and a weight block detail of at least 90 lbs. It requires leveling on slopes steeper than 1/2 in. per foot.
clean.notes:
1. 36 in. square (SQ.) x 1/4 in. thick (THK.) steel platform, hot dip galvanized per ASTM 123.
2. Type 1 base with 4 1 in. diameter x 3-1/2 in. bolts and nuts with 2 washers for each bolt.
3. 3/8 in. diameter steel coil chain tied to each 5 gal. block and locked around the Type 8 standard (and the Type 1 base in the top view detail).
4. 5 gal. can filled with concrete. Four cans are required, spaced as shown.
5. 2 in. high x 1/4 in. thick perimeter lip resting on ground.
6. 1-3/4 in. x 1-3/4 in. x 1/4 in. steel angle brackets welded to plate.
7. 4 holes at 1-1/4 in. diameter. 8-1/2 in. diameter bolt circle.
8. 1 in. x 1 in. notches for cable.
9. For slopes greater than 1/2 in. rise per foot, temporary standard to be set level through the use of grading or wood shims.
10. Weight block: 5 gal. can filled with concrete, minimum weight 90 lbs. 1/2 in. diameter steel rod embedded 9 in. deep. LADOT or contractor name embossed or welded on at least two sides.
Label: 337 cabinet. Base assembly. Lip.
clean.description:
Elevation: a Type 8 standard carrying a 337 cabinet (traffic signal controller cabinet), drawn with the pole cut by break marks. The cabinet is a tall rectangular enclosure with a door handle, ventilation louvers and a City of Los Angeles label plate on the door. It sits on top of the pole and is called out as 337 Cabinet. At the bottom, two 5 gal. concrete blocks sit on a platform with a 3/8 in. diameter steel coil chain tied to each block and locked around the Type 8 standard. The base assembly is bolted to the platform, which has a 2 in. high lip and a LADOT name, a 1 in. x 1 in. notch for cable, and a note for slopes greater than 1/2 in. rise per foot.

Platform, top view detail (not to scale): a 36 in. x 36 in. square steel platform with four 5 gal. cans at the corners, a Type 1 base at the center with 4 bolts, and chain tied through the cans around the standard. Platform, bottom view detail (not to scale): 36 in. x 36 in. with steel angle brackets framing the underside, 4 holes at 1-1/4 in. diameter on an 8-1/2 in. diameter bolt circle, and 1 in. x 1 in. notches for cable at the lip.

Weight block (not to scale): a 5 gal. can filled with concrete, 12 in. wide by 14 in. tall, with a 1/2 in. diameter steel rod loop embedded 9 in. deep at 4 in. spacing and 3 in. above the can. Minimum weight 90 lbs. LADOT or contractor name is embossed or welded on at least two sides.
