clean.title: Fittings, Typical, Post Top Mounting
clean.summary: Drawing S-61.1 shows the typical post top mounting fittings, a slip fitter with six 3/8 in.-16 galvanized square head cup point set screws and a 72-tooth lock ring. The lock ring height is 5/16 in. One note requires construction, materials and finish painting to follow the State of California Standard Specifications.
clean.notes:
1. Construction, material and finish painting shall conform to 'Standard Specifications', (latest edition), Dept. of Transportation, State of California.
Callouts: 72 teeth (slip fitter and lock ring). 3/8 in.-16 N.C. x 3/4 in. square head (Sq. Hd.) cup point (pt.) set screw, hot dip galvanized, (6) required (REQ.). Dimension 5/16 in.
clean.description:
Slip fitter: an isometric view of a cylindrical slip fitter that slides over a post top. It is a stack of two round collars, an upper and a lower, on a central cylinder, with a smaller round post top projecting from the upper surface. The top rim of the projecting post has a toothed edge with 72 teeth. Two square-head set screws are shown on the side at the upper and lower collars. A callout reads 3/8 in.-16 N.C. x 3/4 in. square head cup point set screw, hot dip galvanized, (6) required.

Lock ring: an isometric view of a ring with a toothed upper rim of 72 teeth, an inner bore with two keyed notches on opposite sides, and a lower rim. A dimension of 5/16 in. is given for the ring height at the right.

clean.title: Special Mast Arm Mountings (Sheet 2 of 2)
clean.summary: Sheet 2 of 2 of drawing S-63.1.4 gives ten notes on the Pelco mast arm mounting items A through E, covering their uses, band sizes and fabrication. Detail A is the 4 1/2 in. square, 1/4 in. aluminum plate with four 3/8 in. holes, a 2 in. center hole and a slot, used for sign box reinforcement.
clean.notes:
1. Item A is the basic mounting design for most mast arm signal installations when standard tenon location on the mast arm cannot be utilized. It uses a 6 in. tenon length with 2 3/8 in. outside diameter for plumbizer mounting.
2. Item B is used for installation of traffic signal heads, except programmed visibility (P.V.) heads, when it is desired to mount them horizontally or to adjust the height vertically by movement of Item E.
3. Item C is used for installation of horizontal or vertical programmed visibility (P.V.) heads. It is equipped with 14 in. arms which allow for replacement of signal lamps located in the rear of the signal head.
4. Item D is used for installation of electric signs.
5. Item E is a standard clamp kit designed to be used for fastening Items B, C and D to mast arms or poles in a vertical or horizontal position.
6. The bottom arms in Items B, C and D are stationary and are held in place with pipe threads and set screws. The upper arms slide along the shaft and are held in place with set screws.
7. The standard 29 in. band for Item A and E fits a 4 in. to 8.6 in. diameter. Band lengths up to 56 in. can be used for larger diameter installations.
8. Items A through E are available from Pelco Products Inc. or equivalent.
9. The 1 1/2 in. x 1 1/2 in. aluminum lock nut shown with Item D is commonly used for signal head and pedestrian head installations.
10. The 4 1/2 in. x 4 1/2 in. x 1/4 in. aluminum plate is used for sign box reinforcement at bracket installation location and must be specially fabricated.
Detail A: 4 1/2 in. x 4 1/2 in. x 1/4 in. aluminum plate, not to scale. 3/4 in. typical. 0.4 in. x 0.2 in. slot. 2 in. diameter hole. 3/8 in. diameter holes.
clean.description:
Notes 1 to 10: ten notes describing mounting items A through E. They are listed in the notes field.

Detail A, 4 1/2 in. x 4 1/2 in. x 1/4 in. aluminum plate (not to scale): a square plate in plan, 4 1/2 in. by 4 1/2 in. It has four 3/8 in. diameter holes near the corners, each 3/4 in. typical from the edges, a central 2 in. diameter hole, and a 0.4 in. x 0.2 in. slot at the side of the central hole.

clean.title: Inductive Loop Installation (Standard Drawing S-70.1A, Sheet 1 of 2)
clean.summary: Standard drawing S-70.1A, sheet 1, shows the layout of a pair of 6 ft round inductive loops spaced 8 ft apart with a twisted lead-in running to a pullbox within 3 ft of the curb face. It gives the winding order (3 clockwise turns per detector) and sawcut slot sections with 3 in or 5 in minimum depth, 1/2 in maximum width, and a limit of 8 wires per slot. Slots are filled with loop sealant to within 1/16 in of the top.
clean.notes:
* Depth of slot not to exceed depth of pavement. For P.C.C. (concrete) surfaces, the minimum cover above loop wire shall be 2.5" minimum.

Notes:
1. Install 3 clockwise turns of loop wire for each detector, unless otherwise shown on signal plan.
2. See LADOT material specification No. 92-081-05 or latest revision.
3. Any non-round shaped loops must conform to all other specifications shown on this standard drawing.

Callouts: Fill slot with loop sealant to within 1/16" of top (do not overfill). Twisted clockwise (at least 2 turn per ft.) into a pair. To pullbox. Direction of traffic flow. Curb face. Pullbox 3'-0" max. from curb face.
clean.description:
Plan view: two round loops, LOOP-1 and LOOP-2, in a lane. Each loop is 6' in diameter and the clear spacing between the two loops is 8'. Traffic flows left to right, shown by an arrow labeled DIRECTION OF TRAFFIC FLOW. The loop wires leave the loops on the inside edges and join into a single lead-in that runs toward the curb. The lead-in crosses the CURB FACE and ends at a PULLBOX that is 3'-0" MAX. from the curb face. Section cut markers A-A are at each loop, B-B at the diagonal wire runs, C-C at the joined lead-in, and D-D across the curb face at the pullbox (D-D is detailed on sheet 2 of S-70.1A).

Winding details (not to scale): LOOP-1 and LOOP-2 are each drawn as three concentric clockwise turns. The lead-in wires from each loop are twisted clockwise into a pair, at least 2 turns per foot, and run to the pullbox. The four ends are numbered 1, 2, 3 and 4 at the pullbox end.

Section A-A (through the loop slot): a sawcut slot filled with loop sealant to within 1/16" of the top (do not overfill). Slot depth is 3" MIN.* and slot width is 1/2" MAX. Three loop wires are stacked at the bottom of the slot (see note 1).

Section B-B (diagonal run between loops): slot depth 5" MIN.*, slot width 1/2" MAX., two wires at the bottom.

Section C-C (joined lead-in): slot depth 5" MIN.*, slot width 1/2" MAX., four wires shown at the bottom, labeled 8 WIRES MAXIMUM PER SAWCUT SLOT.

clean.title: Inductive Loop Installation (Standard Drawing S-70.1A, Sheet 2 of 2)
clean.summary: Standard drawing S-70.1A, sheet 2, shows how to connect inductive loop wires to a pullbox with a conduit and stub-out in the street. It gives the pavement opening limits (at least 42 in from the curb face, 18 in from the gutter, no more than 12 in by 16 in), conduit type and depth (2 in PVC at least 18 in deep) and the patch and sealant materials. A five step installation order and a limit of 8 loops or 16 wires per stub-out are also given.
clean.notes:
Notes: Perform loop installation in the following order:
1. Open the pavement at least 42" from curb face and at least 18" from edge of gutter using a star drill or a jack hammer (asphalt concrete only). Open no more than a 12" x 16" area. In cases where there is a concrete bus pad adjacent to the gutter, install the stubout beyond the edge of the bus pad.
2. Install 2" PVC (SC80) or PVC flex (SC40) from the pullbox pit with a 45 degree elbow at the stub-out as shown. Depth of the conduit shall be at least 18" below the street grade.
3. Patch street using hot patch asphalt concrete and sand as shown.
4. Install duct seal where wires enter 2" PVC or 2" PVC flex.
5. Fill sawcut slot with Caltrans approved hot-melt rubberized asphalt sealant.
* No more than 8 loops or 16 wires per stub-out.
clean.description:
Section D-D (not to scale): a cut through the curb, gutter and roadway at the pullbox. At left, the pullbox pit with its lid and the curb and gutter, with sidewalk paving, sits on rock base. A 2" PVC or 2" PVC FLEX conduit leaves the bottom of the pullbox, curves under the curb and gutter and runs to the stub-out in the street. The pavement opening is at least 42" MIN. from the curb face and at least 18" MIN. from the edge of the gutter. A hot patch asphalt concrete patch is placed in the opening, which is 16" MAX. wide. Existing pavement lies on both sides.

Conduit detail (not to scale): a longitudinal section at the stub-out. Existing pavement is at left and right, with HOT PATCH ASPHALT CONCRETE 4" thick over 1" of SAND in the opening. A 2" PVC or 2" PVC FLEX conduit rises at 45 degrees from a minimum 18" below the street surface through sub base and exits at the surface, where the loop wires (marked *) continue horizontally into the sawcut slot filled with LOOP SEALANT. Labels: existing pavement, sub base, sand, loop sealant, loop wires, hot patch asphalt concrete.

Stub-out detail, top view (not to scale): a rectangular hot patch asphalt concrete patch within existing pavement, 16" MAX. long and 12" MAX. wide. A PVC conduit enters from the left as dashed lines and ends in the patch.

clean.title: Bicycle Detector (S-70.1D)
clean.summary: LADOT standard drawing S-70.1D for bicycle detector loops. Case I uses two 3 ft loops spaced 3 ft apart for bicycle-only bike lanes and Case II uses two 6 ft loops spaced 8 ft apart for bicycle and vehicle detection, each with a pullbox no more than 3 ft from the curb face. The sheet also gives loop winding details, saw cut sections A-A through E-E, and nine notes.
clean.notes:
Notes:
1. Install four (4) complete alternating turns of loop wires, unless otherwise specified.
2. For stub-out and conduit details refer to page 2 of S-70.1A.
3. See LADOT Material Specification No. 92-081-05 or latest revision.
4. Use Case I loops for bike lane installations. Use Case II loops when vehicular loops are intended to detect bicycles.
5. An octagonal shaped loop or other non-round shaped loop may be used instead of the round-loop with prior LADOT approval.
6. Same winding pattern to be used in both loops for Case 1 with 1 pair from each loop leading to the pullbox.
7. Loops installed in bike lanes with parking shall be placed with the near edge of the loop 1' to the right of the bike lane delineation line, unless otherwise specified.
8. Loops installed in bike lanes adjacent to the roadside without parking shall be centered in the bike lane, or between the gutter and the bike delineation line, unless otherwise specified.
9. Any LADOT approved non-round shaped loops must conform to all other specifications shown on this standard drawing.
* Depth of slot not to exceed depth of pavement.
Labels: Winding detail (not to scale); Loop 1; Loop 2; twisted clockwise (at least 2 turns per ft.) into a pair; to pullbox; curb face; pullbox; 3'-0" maximum (MAX.); direction of traffic flow; Case I (bicycle only); Case II (bicycle and vehicle).
clean.description:
Winding detail (not to scale): Four loop sketches across the top, labeled LOOP 1 and LOOP 2 for each of the two cases. In each, the loop wire is wound in concentric turns with direction arrows. The two lead-in wires leave each loop and are TWISTED CLOCKWISE (AT LEAST 2 TURNS PER FT.) INTO A PAIR, then run TO PULLBOX. The four wires are numbered 1, 2, 3 and 4 at the bottom. The left pair of sketches (Case I, bicycle only) shows the same multi-turn alternating winding on both loops. The right pair (Case II) shows Loop 1 wound as simple round turns and Loop 2 wound with the alternating spiral pattern.

Case I (bicycle only), plan view: Two circular loops, LOOP 1 and LOOP 2, are each 3' in diameter and spaced 3' apart (3', 3', 3' string across the top). Each loop is cut as a circle with a diagonal saw cut for the lead-in. The two diagonal saw cuts join in a Y and run as a single saw cut across the curb face to a PULLBOX. The pullbox is 3'-0" MAX. from the CURB FACE. The direction of traffic flow arrow points to the right between the two case views. Section cut marks are shown on the plan: A-A and B-B on the loop circles, C-C on the diagonal lead-ins and D-D on the stem leading to the pullbox.

Case II (bicycle and vehicle), plan view: Two circular loops, each 6' in diameter, spaced 8' apart (6', 8', 6' string). The same Y-shaped lead-in leads to a pullbox 3'-0" MAX. from the curb face. Section marks: E-E on Loop 1, A-A and B-B on Loop 2, C-C on the diagonal lead-ins and D-D on the stem.

Saw cut sections (all show a hatched pavement with a narrow slot and wires in the slot): Sect. A-A: slot 3/8" wide, 3.5" deep*, four wires stacked in a single column. Sect. B-B: slot 1/2" wide, 5" deep*, eight wires in two columns of four. Sect. C-C: slot 3/8" wide, 5" deep*, two wires at the bottom. Sect. D-D: slot 1/2" MAX wide, 5" deep*, four wires, with the callout 8 WIRES MAX. PER 1/2" SAWCUT. Sect. E-E: slot 1/2" MAX wide, 5" deep*, three wires. The footnote reads * DEPTH OF SLOT NOT TO EXCEED DEPTH OF PAVEMENT.

clean.title: Preformed Loop Installation (Standard Drawing S-70.1E)
clean.summary: Standard drawing S-70.1E shows a preformed 6 ft inductive loop built from 3/4 in O.D. hose with expansion joints, CPVC tees and cross, and a 3/8 in O.D. asphalt filled lead-in hose. It gives the winding details, a section from the pullbox through a 2 in Schedule 80 PVC conduit to the loop, and seven notes covering materials, #16 TFFN wire with four turns, sealing with rubberized asphalt, and expansion joints. The pullbox is within 3 ft of the curb face.
clean.notes:
1. Pre-formed loop shall be constructed from 1/2" I.D. polypropylene, with an O.D. of 3/4" inch.
2. Loop is to have one continuous #16 TFFN wire through the loop head and lead-in to prevent loop malfunction due to splicing. Loop shall have four (4) turns of wire.
3. The conduit shall be completely filled with hot, rubberized asphalt which will allow the loop to retain flexibility once cooled, prevent incursion of moisture and set the wire turns firmly in place.
4. Each loop head shall be provided with a 5" contraction/expansion joint to allow for movement of pavement and to prevent breakage of the wire and/or conduit. The joint is to have a 9" long by 3/4" Schedule 80 PVC cover slide to be placed over the joint for protection from the elements.
5. Encase lead-in wires in a non-conductive 250 psi flex hose seamless fiber braid reinforcement and a non-conductive seamless extruded urethane non-perforated jacket. Fill lead-in hose completely with hot rubberized asphalt. Twist wires at least two times per foot for entire run. Attach lead-in to loop head with a Schedule 80 CVPC tee and a CVPC adapter bushing.
6. Any variation to the installation as described above shall be approved by the design engineer prior to installation.
7. The 3/8" O.D. lead-in hose shall be installed in 2" PVC conduit between pullbox and entry to pavement slab. Loop shall be attached to top of reinforcing bars when used in the pavement slab.

Callouts: Expansion joint. CPVC tee. CPVC cross. 3/4" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose. 3/8" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose. Twisted tail. Twisted clockwise (at least 2 turn per ft.) into a pair. To pullbox. Detector loop conductors. Schedule 80 PVC 2" conduit (see note 7). Pavement. 4" min.
clean.description:
Plan view: a 6' diameter preformed loop, drawn as a dashed circle with a dashed diagonal bar, connected by a dashed lead-in to a PULLBOX that is 3'-0" MAX. from the CURB FACE. Section A-A is cut along the lead-in path.

Preformed loop detail: the loop is a circular ring built from 3/4" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose, with four expansion joints and CPVC (chlorinated PVC) tees and a CPVC cross on the ring, a diagonal 3/4" O.D. hose across the ring, and a 3/8" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose lead-in leaving at the CPVC cross, ending in a twisted tail.

Winding details (not to scale): the wire is wound in several clockwise turns inside the loop, with the ends twisted clockwise (at least 2 turn per ft.) into a pair and run TO PULLBOX. The two ends are marked 1 and 2.

Section A-A (typical, not to scale): from the pullbox at left, DETECTOR LOOP CONDUCTORS pass from the pullbox through a Schedule 80 PVC 2" conduit (see note 7), under the curb and gutter, then in a 3/8" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose to the detector, within the pavement, running PER PLAN to the loop. The loop sits in the pavement with 4" MIN. between the pavement surface and the loop.

clean.summary: Standard drawing S-70.2 shows how to hook up one to four detector loops to a 2, 3 or 4 pair lead-in cable. clean.notes:

2. The detector lead-in cable can be wired in either a single, double, triple or quadruple channel configuration.
3. Electrical connections shall be carefully soldered and waterproofed.
4. See LADOT material specification No. 92-082-03 or latest revision.
5. Loop numbers shown are typical.
6. System loops use a single pair for each loop.

In every diagram a drain wire leaves the cable and is connected to earth ground at the controller cabinet.

One-loop hookup, 2 pair cable: loop 1 is connected by its twisted pair to the cable. At the far end the pairs are BLUE/WHITE (PAIR 1) and ORANGE/WHITE (PAIR 2). The loop uses one pair. Label: DO NOT CONNECT UNUSED PAIR. Drain wire connected to earth ground at controller cabinet.

Two-loop hookup, 2 pair cable: loops 1 and 2 each connect by a twisted pair to the cable. Pairs: BLUE/WHITE (PAIR 1) and ORANGE/WHITE (PAIR 2). Drain wire connected to earth ground at controller cabinet.

Three-loop hookup, 3 pair cable: loops 1, 2 and 3 each connect by a twisted pair. Pairs: BLUE/WHITE (PAIR 1), ORANGE/WHITE (PAIR 2), GREEN/WHITE (PAIR 3). Drain wire connected to earth ground at controller cabinet.

Four-loop hookup, 4 pair cable: loops 1 to 4 each connect by a twisted pair. Pairs: BLUE/WHITE (PAIR 1), ORANGE/WHITE (PAIR 2), GREEN/WHITE (PAIR 3), BROWN/WHITE (PAIR 4). Drain wire connected to earth ground at controller cabinet.

clean.title: Light Rail Train (LRT) Track Detector Loop (Standard Drawing S-70.4A, Sheet 2 of 3)
clean.summary: Standard drawing S-70.4A, sheet 2, shows the detector loop for new embedded light rail track, a 30 in circular preformed loop with 4 turns of wire between the rails and a 36 in lead to a type A handhole. A 2 in Schedule 80 PVC conduit 30 in deep runs to the termination pullbox. No rebar or other metal except the rails may be within 3 ft of the loop. Six notes cover the preformed loop materials.
clean.notes:
Notes (new track, embedded):
1. Preformed loop to be used for new installations in embedded track.
2. No rebar or metal of any kind other than the track rails shall be placed within three feet (3') horizontally or vertically from LRT loop.
3. See page 2 and 3 for preformed LRT loop details.

LRT preformed loop details, notes:
1. Pre-formed loop shall be constructed from 1/2" I.D. polypropolene, with an O.D. of 3/4 inch.
2. Loop is to have one continuous #16 TFFN wire through the loop head and lead-in to prevent loop malfunction due to splicing. Loop shall have four (4) turns of wire.
3. The conduit shall be completely filled with hot, rubberized asphalt which will allow the loop to retain flexibility once cooled, prevent incursion of moisture and set the wire turns firmly in place.
4. Each loop head shall be provided with a 5" contraction/expansion joint to allow for movement of pavement and to prevent breakage of the wire and/or conduit. The joint is to have a 9" long by 3/4" schedule 80 PVC cover slide to be placed over the joint for protection from the elements.
5. Encase lead-in wire in a non-conductive 250 psi flex hose, seamless, with fiber braid reinforcement and a non-conductive seamless extruded urethane non-perforated jacket. Fill lead-in hose completely with hot rubberized asphalt. Twist wires at least two times per foot for entire run. Attach lead-in to loop head with a schedule 80 CVPC tee and a CVPC adapter bushing.
6. Any variation to the installation as described above shall be approved by the design engineer prior to installation.

A lead 36" long runs from the loop down to a detector handhole type 'A', then horizontally to a termination pullbox with two conduits leaving it. Section A-A is cut at the handhole.

The detector handhole type 'A' connects by 2" PVC Sched. 80 conduit, 30" deep, to the termination pull box, with 30" min. cover at the pull box.

LRT preformed loop details: a block of text notes (notes 1 to 6) on materials and installation of the preformed loop. Continues on sheet 3 of 3.

This sheet is Standard Drawing S-70.4A, Light Rail Train (LRT) Track Detector Loop, sheet 3 of 3.

LRT preformed loop details (cont'd), loop: a circular loop 30" in diameter made of 3/4" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose, with an expansion joint and a CVCC tee on the ring. A 3/8" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose runs from the tee to the Type A Handhole and ends in a twisted tail.

Winding details (not to scale): the wire is wound in four clockwise turns around the loop. The ends are twisted clockwise (at least 2 turns per ft.) into a pair and run to the Type A Handhole, ends labeled 1 and 2.

Type 'A' LRT detector handhole, section: a precast reinforced concrete box with a 9" throat diameter, set under a cast iron frame and cover at the surface. Overall height is 12" from the surface to the bottom of the box, with a box internal depth of 11-3/8", 8" min. clear depth below the cover and a 6" min. clean, crushed rock sump below the box. The backfill at the surface is ballast, PCC or hot AC to match adjacent roadbed material, with a loop sealant layer 4" min. at the top. The box sits in Portland cement concrete, 3" min. around the handhole. Box width is 10-3/8" with 1" walls. Cables of shielded loop conductor pairs enter at the side and splices are made inside the handhole. Conduit to termination pullbox is 2" Schedule 80 PVC, 30" deep, entering through the bottom.

Handhole cover, plan: a cast iron frame and cover with a cross hatched top and a rectangular label reading LADOT. Cover diameter is 11-1/8" and the overall frame diameter is 14-1/4".

clean.title: Metal Cover Traffic Pull Box (Caltrans Pullbox No. 6 (T))
clean.summary: Drawing S-78.5.2 showing the plan and section of the LADOT metal cover traffic pull box, equivalent to Caltrans Pullbox No. 6 (T). It has a reinforced 1/2 in. minimum galvanized steel cover marked TRAFFIC SIGNAL on a Z-bar frame, a concrete footing, a bonding jumper to the conduit grounding bushings and a 1 in. crushed rock base. Metal covered boxes are required in driveways, alleys and where vehicles travel. Remaining details follow Caltrans Standard Plan ES-8.
clean.notes:
NOTES:
1. Traffic pullboxes in driveways, alleys and locations with vehicular traffic shall be metal covered per this standard.
2. Pullbox details not shown on this plan shall conform to Caltrans Standard Plan ES-8.
3. Traffic pullbox shall be provided with steel cover and special concrete footing. Steel cover shall have embossed non-skid pattern.
4. Galvanized conduits must be bonded with copper ground strap around the neck of each conduit. PVC conduits must have their #8 green ground wires spliced together.
5. Top of pull boxes shall be flush with surrounding grade or top of adjacent curb, except that in unpaved areas where pull box is not immediately adjacent to and protected by a concrete foundation, pole or other protective construction, the box shall be placed with its top 1 1/4" above surrounding grade. Where practicable, pull boxes shown in the vicinity of curbs shall be placed adjacent to the back of curb, and pull boxes shown adjacent to standards shall be placed on side of foundation facing away from traffic, unless otherwise noted. When pull box is installed in sidewalk area, the depth of the pull box shall be adjusted so that the top of the pull box is flush with the sidewalk.
6. Pull box cover shall be marked as "TRAFFIC SIGNAL".
7. Bonding jumper for metal covers shall be flat braided strap, 2' long minimum, Panduit Part # BS202446EU or equivalent.
8. Hold-down bolt shall be 5/8" and coarse threaded.

Callouts: Lift hole. Hold-down bolt. Pull box reinforced with galvanized Z-bar welded frame. Reinforced 1/2" minimum (MIN) steel plate cover, galvanized after fabrication, see Notes 3 and 6. Galvanized Z-bar welded frame. Pull box. Bonding jumper, see Note 7. PCC (portland cement concrete). Grounding bushing. 1/2" length sleeve nut with brass bolt. Top flush with finished grade (see Note 5). 6" MIN all around. 3" MIN all around. 1" crushed rock.
clean.description:
Plan view of cover: A rounded-rectangle steel cover with the text 'TRAFFIC SIGNAL' embossed across it. A lift hole is at the left of the text and a hold-down bolt (hex head) at each of the left and right edges, the right one noted 'Hold-down bolt See Note 8'. The outer frame is 2'-11 1/2" +/- long and the cover is 2'-9" +/- long. The overall width is 2'-6" +/- 1" with a 1'-8" +/- inner width. A dashed inner outline marks the plate, dimensioned 1'-11 1/2" +/- by 1'-5" +/- 1". Callouts: Lift hole. Hold-down bolt. Pull box reinforced with galvanized Z-bar welded frame. Reinforced 1/2" MIN steel plate cover, galvanized after fabrication, See Notes 3 & 6.

Section: A cross section of the pull box set in the ground. A galvanized Z-bar welded frame carries the steel plate cover, which is flush with finished grade ('Top flush with finished grade (See Note 5)'). The cover is secured with a 1/2" length sleeve nut with brass bolt. A pull box concrete shell (PCC) surrounds the box, with a stepped lower edge. A bonding jumper (See Note 7) connects from the cover to the conduit grounding bushings, shown as a looped braided strap. Two conduits enter at an angle through the bottom with grounding bushings, and the box rests on a bed of 1" crushed rock. Dimensions: 1'-0" MIN wall depth below grade, 2" and 6" MIN at the footing step, 6" MIN all around and 3" MIN all around for the special concrete footing outside the box.

clean.title: Composite Pull Box, Types PB-2 & PB-3
clean.summary: LADOT standard drawing S-78.5.3 for a polymer concrete pull box for non-traffic areas, with a non-skid cover marked TRAFFIC SIGNAL. It shows installation in section and side view, the cover plan, captive bolt and threaded insert details, an exploded isometric, and a dimensions table for Types PB2 and PB3. Boxes may be stacked no more than two deep.
clean.notes:
Notes:
1. Refer to Dept. of Public Works Standard Drawing # L-201-1 for additional details and requirements.
2. Galvanized conduits in pull box must be bonded with copper ground strap around the neck of each conduit. PVC conduits must have their #8 green ground wires spliced together.
3. Pull box to be used in non-traffic areas, may be stacked no more than two deep.
4. Stencil TRAFFIC SIGNAL in 1" lettering on backside of cover and inside of box.
Callouts: Top flush with finished grade; 1" crushed rock; see Note 2; TRAFFIC SIGNAL, 7/8" letters; 4" x 1/2" pull slot with 3/16" center pin; manufacturer's logo; load rating; recess in cover for hardware (X2); 1/2"-13 coarse thread stainless steel penta head bolt; stainless steel flat washer; cast-in bolt gripper; 1/2"-13 unified national coarse thread jam nut with threadlocker; insert with drainage hole; drainage hole; polymer concrete cover; non skid surface; polymer concrete box; open base; 3" x 4-1/4" mouse hole knockouts both end (2X).
clean.description:
Section A-A (installation details, Detail A): A polymer concrete pull box set in the ground with its top flush with finished grade (callout TOP FLUSH WITH FINISHED GRADE). The box is shown in two stacked pieces, the lower box and an extension, with the cover on top. The depth of the upper section is labeled D and the lower extension E. The inside length is labeled LI. Two conduits enter low through the walls from either side, curving up into the box through mouse hole knockouts, bedded in 1" Crushed rock. A "See Note 2" callout points to the conduit ends in the box. Dimensions at the conduit ends: 5" Min and 2" Min vertical, 2" Min horizontal, and a 6" Min dimension outside the box wall.

Side view: The same pull box seen from the side, section marks A at the top and bottom, top flush with finished grade over a crushed rock base. The inside width is labeled WI.

Cover top view: A rounded rectangle, length L and width W, with a 1-3/8" corner dimension. Features: TRAFFIC SIGNAL in 7/8" LETTERS in the center, two 4" x 1/2" PULL SLOT WITH 3/16" CENTER PIN, MANUFACTURER'S LOGO, LOAD RATING, and RECESS IN COVER FOR HARDWARE (X2) at two diagonal corners. A cutaway shows the non-skid surface texture.

Typical cover captive bolt (or similar): A bolt through the cover with callouts 1/2"-13 COARSE THREAD STAINLESS STEEL PENTA HEAD BOLT, STAINLESS STEEL FLAT WASHER, CAST-IN BOLT GRIPPER, and 1/2"-13 UNIFIED NATIONAL COARSE THREAD JAM NUT WITH THREADLOCKER. Cover thickness is labeled TE, edge distance B, and a 1/8" dimension is shown.

Typical threaded insert (or similar): A section through the cover edge showing an INSERT WITH DRAINAGE HOLE and a DRAINAGE HOLE.

Isometric view: An exploded view of the POLYMER CONCRETE COVER (with NON SKID SURFACE) above the POLYMER CONCRETE BOX with OPEN BASE and 3" X 4-1/4" MOUSE HOLE KNOCKOUTS BOTH END (2X).

Nominal dimensions table: Columns are Pull box type, Minimum depth box (D), Minimum depth extension (E), LI Min, WI Min, then Cover columns TE, B, L, W.
Row PB2: D 12", E 10", LI Min 1'-8", WI Min 11", TE 2", B 1-3/4", L 1'-11-1/4", W 1'-1-3/4".
Row PB3: D 12", E 10", LI Min 2'-4-1/4", WI Min 1'-3-1/4", TE 2", B 2", L 2'-6-1/2", W 1'-5-1/2".

clean.summary: Drawing S-78.8 showing the galvanized steel special frame and cover for Type 2 and Type 3 pull boxes in sidewalk. Plan, elevation, an 8 degree sloped-edge section and a lift plug detail are given, with a table of dimensions A to G for each pull box type. The cover is 3/16 in. plate with brass lift plugs and stamped SIGNAL lettering, set flush with sidewalk grade on a 4 in. x 3/16 in. steel plate frame.
clean.notes:
Notes:
1. All metal surfaces for special frame and cover shall have a galvanized finish.
2. All welding, machining and drilling shall be done before galvanizing.
3. Plug threads must be greased thoroughly prior to installation.

Callouts: 2-3/4" brass lift plug. 1" stamped letters (revision 2). 1/2" x 1/2" continuous steel bar. Steel sleeve internal thread 3/4"-10 UNC full length to match brass lift plug. Slot 3/8" square and 3/8" deep. 4" x 3/16" steel plate typical all sides. Typical all four (4) sides of frame and cover. End and mid-point (typical). Sidewalk grade. Pull box.
clean.description:
Plan view: A rectangular special cover seen from above inside its frame, with a wavy break line showing the cover cut away at the right. 'SIGNAL' is lettered at the center and a centerline passes through two lifting holes marked '2-3/4" Brass lift plug'. Callout 2 (revision triangle) points to '1" Stamped letters'. Variable dimensions are lettered: "A" is the cover outside width, "B" the frame inside width, "C" the frame inside length, "D" the distance from the top edge of the frame to the centerline. A 4" typical band marks the steel plate frame width.

Cover elevation: The cover is dimensioned "E" overall at the top with 3" typical from the end to each lift plug, and "F" at the bottom, with a beveled (sloped) edge. Cover thickness is 1 13/16".

Section through frame and cover (8 degree detail): The frame and cover edges are sloped at 8 degrees from vertical on all four sides. A 3/16" plate forms the cover and a 4" x 3/16" steel plate forms the frame, with 1/8" typical clearance between them. The cover rests on a 1/2" x 1/2" continuous steel bar, welded with a 3/16" fillet weld, 3" long, at the end and mid-point (typical). The height shown is 1 13/16".

Lift plug detail: A steel sleeve with internal thread 3/4"-10 UNC, full length, to match the brass lift plug. The plug has a 3/8" square slot, 3/8" deep. The cover plate is 3/16" steel plate and the plug depth is 5/8" with 3/16" below, within a total thickness of 1 13/16". A 3/16" weld symbol is shown at the sleeve.

Section in sidewalk: The frame sits flush with sidewalk grade over the pull box. Dimensions: "C" frame inside across the top, "G" frame inside across the base, 1 13/16", 2 3/16" and 4" depths, a 1/2" x 1/2" continuous steel bar, and 4" x 3/16" steel plate typical on all sides. Concrete surrounds the frame above the pull box.

Table of dimensions:
For Type 2 Pullbox: A = 18 3/4", B = 19", C = 29", D = 9 1/2", E = 28 3/4", F = 28 1/4", G = 27 7/8".
For Type 3 Pullbox: A = 25 3/4", B = 26", C = 38", D = 13", E = 37 3/4", F = 37 1/4", G = 36 7/8". Revision 1 applies to the table.

clean.summary: Drawing S-52.1 showing the LADOT Type F-1 and F-8 signal and lighting pole foundation, a 24 in. x 24 in. (24 in. diameter optional) concrete footing 42 in. deep with four 1 in. anchor bolts on an 8 1/2 in. bolt circle, a 10 in. x 10 in. x 3/4 in. base plate and a mortar bed. 2. Type F-8 and Type F-8A: 3" nominal size conduit, unless otherwise specified.

Callouts: 0.50" NC square nut holder with fastener for grounding welded to interior of pole shaft at 180 degrees from hand hole rim. #8 green bonding wire. Anchor bolt: thread top 8" and galvanize 12" (2 nuts and 2 washers required per bolt), total 4. Base plate 10" x 10" x 3/4". 2" minimum to 3" maximum mortar. Curb face. clean.description:

A 4-bolt pattern lies at the center of the middle 24" square on an 8 1/2" bolt circle, with diagonals at 45 degrees to the centerline. A dashed conduit stub runs from the center to the right side of the slab. Callouts: 4" thick slab (two places), 8 1/2" bolt circle, Curb Face.

Elevation: A pole stands on a 10" x 10" x 3/4" base plate with 1" diameter anchor bolts, set on mortar over a concrete footing. The pole carries a 3" x 5" reinforced hand hole and cover, with the hand hole rim 1" +/- 1/4" above the base plate level and 8" above finished grade. A 0.50" NC square nut holder with fastener for grounding is welded inside the pole shaft at 180 degrees from the hand hole rim, and a #8 green bonding wire runs from it down to the anchor bolt. The mortar bed between base plate and footing is 2" minimum (MIN.) to 3" maximum (MAX.) thick and is finished with a slope from 45 degrees to 90 degrees including drain holes. A curb face is shown at the left. The footing is 24" x 24" (24" diameter optional) and 42" deep, with a 4" minimum topping (minimum 14" MIN. dimension from grade to the conduit elbow) and a 3" MIN. dimension at the bottom of the footing. Anchor bolts are 1" diameter x 3'-0" long with the bottom 6" threaded, and an anchor plate 10" x 10" x 3/4" at the bottom, with 2 nuts and 2 washers each. A conduit rises in the center and bends to exit the side (See notes 1 and 2).

clean.summary: Drawing S-79.8 showing an overhead service from a Department of Water and Power (DWP) pole to a PB-3 service pullbox. DWP brings 3 #2 aluminum wires down the pole in a 2 in. conduit and splices 12 in. #6 copper tails, which feed in-line 60 Amp fuses for the traffic signal, bonded neutral and 3 #6 wires for street lighting. The pullbox is 5 to 15 ft from the pole and 14 in. minimum deep, with a ground rod and bonding wire.
clean.notes:
Notes:
1. Department of Water and Power (DWP) to install 3 #2 stranded aluminum wires from service pole to pullbox. At the terminus of each #2 aluminum wire the Department of Water and Power to splice 2 #6 stranded copper wires, (12" long) using compression type connectors. The exposed ends of each copper wire shall be taped when not in use.
2. Install continuous and dedicated #6 green service ground conductor to controller cabinet.
3. See Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction, Sec. 307-2.8.

clean.description:
Wiring diagram: Across the top is a Pullbox Cover labeled 'Service T.S. & S.L.' (traffic signal and street lighting). Below it, three 'Alum. wires by DWP' (3 #2) drop from the service pole, the center one marked Neutral. At the end of each, 6 #6 standard copper wires (12" long) by DWP are spliced. Each of the two outer legs splits into two copper wires, each with a 60 Amp fuse in-line waterproof fuseholder for traffic signals, giving #6 traffic signal service wires, and a #6 spare for traffic signal (when specified) on the right leg. The neutral leg is bonded to the ground rod (Bond neutral to ground rod) and continues as the neutral service wire. 3 #6 wires for B.S.L. clean.description:

Two 3" conduits (2-3" CONDUITS) rise into the cabinet from the foundation. clean.title: Service Grounding Conduit System (PVC and Galvanized)
clean.summary: Drawing S-79.9B showing two schematics of service grounding, one for PVC conduit and one for galvanized conduit, running from a service pullbox through a controller pullbox to the traffic signal cabinet. Each carries dedicated #6 black, #6 green and #6 white service wires with a #8 green bond wire, with 8 ft x 1/2 in. ground rods at the service and the cabinet. A ground rod wire clamp (Acorn) is used for each wire, and bushings are required on all metal conduit.
clean.notes:
* Note (both diagrams): Use a ground rod wire clamp for each wire (Acorn).

PVC Conduit System callouts: Service pullbox. Service fuse. Bonded galvanized conduit. NC. From utility AC+, AC-, AC+. #8 green bond wire. Schedule 80 PVC. Service ground rod: 8FT x 1/2". Dedicated service #6 black, #6 green, #6 white. Black, Green, White. Controller pullbox. Compression type fitting. Traffic signal cabinet. Cabinet service block (Ground, AC+, AC-). Equipment ground bus. Cabinet ground rod: 8FT x 1/2".

Galvanized Conduit System callouts: Use a bushing on all metal conduit. Bonded galvanized conduit. Other callouts as in the PVC system.
clean.description:
PVC Conduit System (top diagram): A schematic of service grounding with a Service Pullbox at left, a Controller Pullbox in the middle and a Traffic Signal Cabinet at right. In the service pullbox, three utility conductors AC+, AC- and AC+ come in 'From Utility' through bonded galvanized conduit to the service fuse. The service ground rod is 8FT x 1/2", and a #8 green bond wire connects the conduit bond to the ground rod (marked with an asterisk, with an NC (normally closed) point). Schedule 80 PVC carries a dedicated service of #6 black, #6 green and #6 white (Black, Green, White) plus a #8 green bond wire to the controller pullbox. In the controller pullbox the wires pass through in Schedule 80 PVC, with the #8 green bond wires joined by a compression type fitting between two PVC stubs. The wires continue in Schedule 80 PVC to the traffic signal cabinet, where black, green and white land on the cabinet service block (Ground, AC+, AC-). The #8 green bond wire goes to the cabinet ground rod (8FT x 1/2") and, through a compression type fitting, to the equipment ground bus.

Galvanized Conduit System (bottom diagram): Same layout, but the conduits between pullboxes are bonded galvanized conduit instead of PVC, with a callout 'Use a bushing on all metal conduit' and 'Bonded Galvanized conduit' at the pullbox ends. The #8 green bond wire connects to the conduit bonding at each pullbox. The controller pullbox has a compression type fitting joining the bond wire to the two PVC stubs, and the cabinet ground rod arrangement is the same as in the PVC system.

clean.title: Sign, Cantilever, 12' Arm Special (Arm Mounting Height 20'-6")
clean.summary: Standard drawing S-98.0 for a special cantilever sign with a 12' arm mounted at 20'-6" above grade. The post is 8" Schedule 80 Grade B pipe and the arm is 6" Schedule 40 Grade B pipe, on a PF-12 caisson 30" in diameter and 10'-0" deep. Design wind loading is 20 psf, with details for the arm connection, arm end cap and base plate, and sign dimensions on S-45.0.
clean.notes:
Specification. Design: Design loading, wind loading 20 pounds per square foot (psf). Design stresses: concrete n = 10, f'c = 3,000 pounds per square inch (psi), fc = 1,200 psi; reinforcing steel fs = 20,000 psi; structural steel fb = 18,000 psi; soil bearing pressure 3,000 psi.

Callouts: Caisson concrete shall be 560-C-3250 (revision 1). Four anchor bolts 1-1/2" dia. x 54" (includes a 6" right angle bend), threaded (thrd.) 8", galvanized (galv.) top 12", 2 hex. nuts and 2 standard (std.) washers each. 3" x 5" hand hole with frame and removable cover, 1" radius corners in hand hole.

General notes:
1. All metal parts shall be galvanized after fabrication.
2. All pipes shall conform to ASTM A53 Grade B.
3. Welding shall be in conformance with AWS specifications "Welded Highway & Railway Bridges", dated 1966, revised 1967.
4. Tapered tube of equivalent size and capacity may be substituted for pipe post subject to the approval of the Engineer.
5. Sign arms shall be made level by raking the standard with the leveling nuts or other method approved by the Engineer to compensate for dead load deflection.
6. All structural steel shall conform to ASTM designation A7 or A36.
7. See S-45.0 for sign dimensions, positioning and mounting.
clean.description:
Elevation: A tall single-post cantilever sign standard shown with the sign arm at the top and a caisson foundation below grade. The post is 8" Schedule 80 Grade B pipe. The arm mounting height is dimensioned 20'-6" from finished grade to the arm centerline, and the post extends 1'-0" above the arm centerline to a removable top cap (Detail "A"). The arm is 6" Schedule 40 Grade B pipe, shown with break lines, projecting to the right across a dashed sign panel outline (also with break lines). The arm end has a cap (Detail "B") and the sign panel extends 2'-6" MAX. beyond the end of the arm. Detail "C" (base) is circled at the foot of the post. A 3'-0" dimension is shown from the post centerline to the edge of the base area and a 3" MIN. dimension is noted at the base. Below grade is the PF-12 foundation, 10'-0" foundation depth, with an 18" MIN. dimension near the top of the caisson, anchor bolts hooked at the bottom, and #5 @ 4" pitch spiral reinforcement with 3" clear. Caisson concrete is called out with a revision triangle 1 as 560-C-3250. Section cut A-A is taken through the caisson.

Detail "A" (arm connection at top of post): Shown in side and plan views. The side view shows the 3/16" PL. (removable top) plate, 9-5/8" wide, with 2 set screws and a plate 2" x 3/16" bent to circular shape with 7-1/4" O.D. welded to the post. The arm attaches to the post by 4 - 3/4" dia. x 4" ASTM A-325 bolts, each with hex nut and 2 hardened 9 ga. washers, through 2 plates 4-3/8" x 5/16" x 13" long. Fillet welds shown: 1/4", 3/8", 3/16" and 1/8" at various joints. Plan-type views show dimensions 1-1/4", 1" and 1-1/2" for plate offsets and thicknesses. The lower view shows the 2 plates 13" x 1/4" x 17" long with (4) 7/8" dia. holes, 2" corner radius (2"R), 2" edge distances, a hole spacing of 13" horizontally and 9" vertically (4-1/2" each side of centerline), a 2" dia. hole finished smooth at the center, 2 gusset plates 5" x 5/16" x 8-5/8" long cut to fit flush, a 3/4" std. half coupling, and 1/4" fillet welds. The sign arm is labeled on the side view.

Detail "B" (arm end cap): 1/4" plate with 1/8" fillet weld, 7-1/8" high (round plate, 7-1/8" dia. in the end view) and a 1" NPT pipe plug at its center.

Detail "C" (base): Section through the base plate and anchorage. Shows a 3" x 5" hand hole with frame and removable cover (1" radius corners in hand hole) in the post wall, four anchor bolts 1-1/2" dia. x 54" (includes a 6" right angle bend), thrd. 8", galv. top 12", with 2 hex. nuts and 2 std. washers each. Vertical dimensions shown include 10", 5", 1-1/4", 1-1/2" and 3-1/2" (base plate to top of concrete). Also shown are a 3/8" dia. drain hole, bonding wire, base plate, and welds of 1/4" and 5/16".

Base Plate (plan): Square plate 14-1/8" sq. with 2"R corners, (4) 1-3/4" dia. holes on a 13-1/2" dia. bolt circle (B.C.), and the post seat 9-9/16" sq.

Section A-A: Circular caisson cross section, 30" pile dia., with 8 #7 x 9'-6" long equally spaced vertical bars, 3" cl. to spiral, with the anchor bolts inside the cage on a 9-9/16" sq. pattern.

Specification block (upper right): Design loading, wind loading 20 psf. Design stresses: concrete n=10, f'c = 3,000 psi, fc = 1,200 psi; reinforcing steel fs = 20,000 psi; structural steel fb = 18,000 psi; soil bearing pressure 3,000 psi.

clean.title: 22' Cantilever Sign Standard Detail (S-92.3)
clean.summary: Standard drawing S-92.3 for a 22' cantilever sign standard. An 8XX-Strong pipe post carries an 8X-Strong pipe arm, on a PF-22 cast-in-drilled-hole foundation 36" in diameter and 10'-0" deep. Total sign area is limited to 90 sq. ft. The sheet gives the arm connection, end cap, anchor bolt, base and reinforcing details and the AASHO 1968 design basis.
clean.notes:
Notes (on elevation):
1. Total sign area shall not exceed 90 square feet (sq. ft.).
2. Length "F" shall not exceed 15.5 feet with maximum sign area.

Specification. Design: American Association of State Highway Officials (A.A.S.H.O.) Specifications for the Design and Construction of Structural Supports for Highway Signs, dated 1968. Loading: wind, normal to sign face: 23.3 psi. Transverse to force: 0.2 of normal force. Unit stresses: structural steel fb = 23,000 psi; reinforcing steel fs = 24,000 psi; concrete n=10, f'c = 3000 psi, fc = 1200 psi; soil bearing pressure c = 3,000 psi.

Detail note: Sign mounting assembly not shown on detail (Detail B). Bolts not shown on plan (Detail A plan).

General notes:
1. All metal parts shall be galvanized after fabrication.
2. All pipes shall conform to ASTM A53 Grade B specification.
3. Welding shall be in conformance with AWS-D2.0 specifications "Welded Highway & Railway Bridges", dated 1969.
4. Tapered tube of equivalent size and capacity may be substituted for pipe post subject to the approval of the Engineer.
5. Sign arms shall be made level by raking the standard with the leveling nuts or other method approved by the Engineer to compensate for dead load deflection.
6. All structural steel shall conform to ASTM designation A36, except as shown on plan.
7. See S-45.0 for sign dimensions, positioning and mounting.
clean.description:
Elevation (not to scale): 22' cantilever sign standard. A vertical post of Pipe 8XX-Strong carries a horizontal sign arm of Pipe 8X-Strong at the top. Overall arm reach from the post centerline is 22'. Dimension F (see note below) runs from the post centerline to the centroid of the sign area. The sign area is a dashed rectangle with break lines, 18' MAX. long, 5' MAX. high, and its end extends 2'-6" MAX. beyond the end of the arm. The post top is 18" above the arm centerline, the arm height above grade is 20'-1" and the overall post height is 21'-7". A 3'-0" dimension locates a curb from the post centerline. The curb top is flush with grade and a 2'-0" MIN. dimension is given below it. Below grade is a PF-22 CIDH (cast-in-drilled-hole) foundation 36" dia., 10'-0" deep, with a 2" conduit to T. S. (traffic signal) pullbox leaving the foundation, see Section A-A for reinforcing. Detail circles A (arm head), B (arm end), C (base at grade) and D (anchor bolt template at the bottom of the bolts) are referenced.

Detail "A" (arm to post connection, not to scale): A plan view shows the post, the arm, 1-1/4" and 1" plate offsets, 1" x 1/4" backing ring, tack weld, 3/8" and 1/8" weld sizes and 5/16" fillet welds, and a note that bolts are not shown on plan. An elevation view shows a Pl. 3/16 x 9-5/8 O.D. (removable top) plate with 2 set screws on the post, a Bar 2 x 3/16 bent to circular shape with 6-3/4" O.D., Pl. 1/2" x 4-7/8" x 1'-2" long (2 required), the sign arm 8-5/8" O.D., the connection plates 14" tall, a 2" dia. hole finished smooth, and 4 - 1-1/4" dia. x 4" ASTM A-325 bolts with hex nut and washer. The post is 8-5/8" O.D. with a 1/4" weld at the base of the connection and 5/16" welds shown. A face view shows Pl 1-1/4" x 14 x 1'-5" long, 2 required, with 4 - 1-1/2" dia. holes, 2" edge distances, 1'-5" overall width with 1'-1" hole spacing, 1'-2" overall height with 10" hole spacing, 2"R (TYP.) corners, Bar 5" x 1/2" x 9" long, 2 required, cut to fit flush, and a 3/4" standard half coupling, with 5/16" fillet welds.

Detail "B" (arm end): End plate Pl. 3/16 x 9" O.D. on the sign arm with a 1/8" fillet weld, shown in side and end views, 9" dia. A note says the sign mounting assembly is not shown on the detail.

Detail "D": Template plate bar with two holes. Dimensions 6-1/2", 6-1/2" and 3" along the length, 2-1/2" width and 1-7/8" dia. holes.

Section A-A (not to scale): Round foundation cross section 36" dia. with a 12-#7 x 9'-6" long equally spaced vertical bars, #4 spiral at 6" pitch, 3" clear. The 4 anchor bolt locations form a rectangle with 1'-6" and 1'-1" dimensions and 2-1/2" edge distances, on a base plate square 1'-6" by 1'-1" with 2"R corners. The center sign line (CL Sign) is marked, with a 3" dia. hole finished smooth at the center and a 2" dia. hole noted.

Detail "C" PF-22 (not to scale): Section through the post base and foundation top. Shows the post, 3" x 5" hand hole with frame and removable cover with 1" radius corners, base plate on mortar at top of walk, 1" x 1/4" backing ring, tack weld, 3/8" dia. drain hole, 4 - 1-3/4" dia. anchor bolts (thrd. 8, galv. top 12", 2 hex nuts and 2 std. washers each, ASTM A-307), banding wire, conduit, and bar 5" x 1" x 1'-7" long (parallel to axis of sign, 2 required) tack welded at the bolt bottoms. Dimensions include 8" and 3/8"/1/8" welds at the hand hole, 2", 4-1/2", 2" and 2'-8" to the bottom of the anchor bolt projection, 1" and 3" typ. Foundation concrete shall be 560-C-3250 (see reinforcement in Sec. A-A). Section marker A points to the Section A-A cut.

Specification block: Design per A.A.S.H.O. Specifications for the Design and Construction of Structural Supports for Highway Signs, dated 1968. Loading: wind normal to sign face 23.3 psi. Transverse to force 0.2 of normal force. Unit stresses: structural steel fb = 23,000 psi, reinforcing steel fs = 24,000 psi, concrete n=10, f'c = 3000 psi, fc = 1200 psi, soil bearing pressure c = 3,000 psi.

clean.title: 34' Cantilever Sign Standard and Foundation Details (Sheet 1 of 2, S-92.2)
clean.summary: Sheet 1 of 2 of standard drawing S-92.2 for a 34' monotube cantilever sign standard. A 14X-Strong pipe post carries two 10 Std. pipe arms, on a 3'-0" dia. PF-34 cast-in-drilled-hole foundation 15' deep. The sheet gives the arm end plate, post cap and arm connection details and the design loading and stresses, with notes and the foundation on sheet 2.
clean.notes:
Specification. Design: American Association of State Highway Officials (A.A.S.H.O.) Specifications for the Design and Construction of Supports for Highway Signs, dated 1968. Loading: wind, normal to sign face: 23.3 pounds per square foot (psf); transverse to face: 0.2 of normal force. Unit stresses: concrete n=10, f'c = 3000 pounds per square inch (psi), fc = 1200 psi; reinforcing steel fs = 24,000 psi; structural steel fb = 23,000 psi; soil bearing pressure = 23,000 psf.

Callouts that refer to notes: Dimension B (See Notes) and Sign (See Notes). The numbered notes are not on this sheet and continue on sheet 2 of 2.

Detail note: See "Weld Detail" (Detail C plan view).
clean.description:
Elevation, Monotube Overhead Sign Supports (not to scale): A 34' cantilever sign standard with a single vertical post of Pipe 14X-Strong and two horizontal arms of Pipe 10 Std. The arms span 34' from the post centerline. Dimension B (see notes) runs from the post centerline to the centroid of the sign area. The sign (see notes) is drawn as a rectangle with vertical stiffener lines between the two arms, and is 6' MAX. high. Vertical dimensions on the post: 18" from the post top to the upper arm centerline, 3' between the two arm centerlines, 21' from grade to the lower arm centerline, and 25-1/2' from grade to the post top. A 3' dimension locates the curb from the post centerline. A 3/4" std. half coupling is on the post. Callouts point to Detail "B" (post top cap), Detail "C" (arm to post connection, at both arms), Detail "A" (arm end plate at both arm ends) and Detail "D" (base, circled at grade). Below grade is a 3'-0" dia. C.I.D.H. (cast-in-drilled-hole) foundation (PF-34), 15' deep with a break line, with see Section A-A for reinforcement.

Detail "A" (arm end): An end plate Pl. 3/16 x 11-1/4 dia. with a 1/8" fillet weld on an arm of 10-3/4" O.D.

Detail "B" (post top): Removable top Pl. 3/16 x 15 dia., 2 set screws, 15" dia. plate, 1" plate offset dimension, Bar 2" x 3/16" bent to circular shape with 12-1/2" O.D. inside the post, 1/8" fillet weld.

Detail "C" (arm to post connection): Plan view shows the post, the arm, Bar 7-3/4" x 1/2" x 14-3/8" long, 2 req'd, cut to fit flush with pipe, 1-1/4" and 1-1/4" plate dimensions, 7" offset, see Weld Detail, Bar 1" x 1/4" backing ring and 5/16" welds. Elevation shows Bar 7" x 1/2" x 14" long, 2 req'd, 4 - 1-1/4" dia. ASTM A-325 bolts with hex. nut and washer, a 1/2" plate thickness dimension, 1/4" gap, and 5/16" and 3/16" welds. A face view shows 2 - Pl 1-1/4" x 14" x 22" long with 2"R typical corners, 22" overall width with 18" bolt spacing and 2" edge distances, 14" height with 10" bolt spacing (5" each side of center) and 2" edge distances, 9" dimension, a 2" dia. hole in plates and pipe finished smooth, a 3/4" std. half coupling, the 14" O.D. post, and 5/16" welds.

Specification block (upper right): Design per A.A.S.H.O. Specifications for the Design and Construction of Supports for Highway Signs, dated 1968. Loading: wind normal to sign face 23.3 psf, transverse to face 0.2 of normal force. Unit stresses: concrete n=10, f'c = 3000 psi, fc = 1200 psi; reinforcing steel fs = 24,000 psi; structural steel fb = 23,000 psi; soil bearing pressure = 23,000 psf.

clean.title: 34' Cantilever Sign Standard and Foundation Details (Sheet 2 of 2, S-92.2)
clean.summary: Sheet 2 of 2 of standard drawing S-92.2 for the 34' cantilever sign standard. It shows the post base, anchor bolts, anchor bars, the 3'-0" dia. cast-in-drilled-hole foundation reinforcement and the base weld. General notes limit sign area to 180 sq. ft. and length B to 22' and set galvanizing, pipe, welding and steel requirements.
clean.notes:
General notes:
1. Total sign area shall not exceed 180 sq. ft.
2. Length "B" shall not exceed 22' with maximum sign area.
3. See plan for positioning of panel.
4. All metal parts shall be galvanized after fabrication.
5. All pipes shall conform to ASTM A53 Grade B specification.
6. Welding shall be in conformance with AWS D2.0 specifications "Welded Highway & Railway Bridges", dated 1969.
7. Tapered tube of equivalent size and capacity may be substituted for pipe post subject to the approval of the Engineer.
8. Sign arms shall be made level by raking the standard with the leveling nuts or other method approved by the Engineer to compensate for dead load deflection.
9. All structural steel shall conform to ASTM designation A36, except where otherwise shown.

Detail callouts: Foundation concrete is 560-C-3250. 3" x 5" hand hole with frame and removable cover, 1" radius corners in hand hole.
clean.description:
Detail "D" (base of post and foundation top, not to scale): Section through the post base and top of the foundation. The post has a 3" x 5" hand hole with frame and removable cover (1" radius corners in hand hole), located with dimensions 10" and 5" above the base plate and 2" at the walk. The base plate sits on mortar at the top of walk, with see "Weld Detail", Bar 1" x 1/4" backing ring and a 3/8" dia. drain hole called out. A 1" +/- dimension is given above the plate for the anchor bolt thread projection. ASTM A-307 anchor bolts 2" dia. x 32" long with nuts and washers, 4 req'd, run down through the concrete foundation 560-C-3250, with a bonding wire, conduit, and bars 5" x 1" x 22" long at the bolt bottoms, parallel to the axis of sign (see Detail "E"), tack welded, 2-1/2" Typ. edge distance. Overall height from the bottom of the bar to the top of the anchor bolt is 2'-8". Section cut markers A point toward Section A-A.

Detail "E" (anchor bar, not to scale): Plan of the bar 5" x 1" x 22" long, 2 req'd, with chamfered ends and two 2-1/8" dia. holes. Dimensions: 22" overall length, 2" Typ. and 2-1/2" Typ. edge distances, 5" width, 2-1/2" Typ. from the bar edge to hole centerline.

Section A-A (not to scale): Plan of the 3'-0" cast in drilled hole foundation with 3" clear to the reinforcing. Shown are 12-#8 x 14-1/2' long bars equally spaced, #4 spiral @ 3-1/4" pitch, a Base Plate PL 2" x 23" x 23" long with 3" dimension to the edge of the 17" bolt pattern, the post centered on the sign centerline (CL Sign), a 3" dia. hole finish smooth and a 2-1/8" dia. hole. Dimensions: 23" plate width, 17" bolt spacing in both directions, 3" edge distances.

Weld Detail (not to scale): The post pipe wall welded to the base plate on a backing ring, with a tack weld on the ring and a fillet weld shown with 1/8 and 3/8 weld legs and a 3/8" dimension.

clean.title: Laminated Overhead Sign Mounting System (S-45.0)
clean.summary: Standard drawing S-45.0 shows how laminated overhead sign panels in an H-edge aluminum frame are mounted on cantilever mast arms using aluminum I-beams, U-bolts and clamps. A table gives maximum panel size, positioning dimensions and U-bolt size for 12', 22' and 34' arms, with a parts list and sign material notes.
clean.notes:
General notes:
1. Overhead sign panels shall be Type "A" laminated sign panel per LADOT Spec. 82-052-01.
2. See LADOT Std. Dwg. Nos. S-92.2, S-92.3, or S-98.0 for dimensions, spacings, quantities, and other requirements dependent on mast arm specifications.
3. All bolts, nuts and washers shall be stainless steel or hot-dipped galvanized in accordance with Section 210-3, Std. Spec. for Public Works Construction (1985 edition).
4. Guide signs shall have a white legend and border made of FP92 Type III (high intensity) reflective material on a green background made of FP92 Type II (super-engineering grade) reflective material.
5. Regulatory signs shall have a black (Scotch-Cal) legend and border, on a white background made of FP92 Type IV (VIP grade) reflective material.

Drawing labels: Y = overall length of U-bolt. "H" edge aluminum frame. Sections and mounting hardware are not to scale.
clean.description:
Plan view: A laminated overhead sign panel in a "H" edge aluminum frame (item 1) seen from above, with the mast arm (item 3, shown dashed behind the panel) running horizontally along the panel centerline from the mast arm flange on the left. Overall panel length is dimension A. Along the top, dimension C is the distance from the left end of the panel to the first I-beam, then I-beam spacing is 6' MAX., and dimension E is the distance from the last I-beam to the right end. Panel height is dimension B, with dimension D locating the arm centerline from the bottom edge, and the arm centerline is shown centered. The I-beams (item 2) run vertically across the panel, attached to the arm by U-bolts (item 4) at two locations. Aluminum straps (item 5) at the panel closures are shown at one vertical joint (4 per closure). Mounting clamps (item 6) and post clip bolts (item 7) are shown at the top and bottom ends of each I-beam. A 2'-6" MAX. dimension is given on the right end. Cut lines A-A, B-B and C-C are marked.

Elevation: Side view below the plan shows the mast arm (item 3) on the left flange with U-bolts and I-beams (item 2) under the arm, over the panel (item 1) shown edge-on.

End view: The panel seen from the arm end, with the arm (item 3) held by U-bolt (item 4), clamps (item 6) and bolts (item 7) at the top and bottom of the I-beam, and the "H" edge aluminum frame. Dimensions B and D are shown.

clean.title: 14' Cantilever Changeable Message Sign (Sheet 1 of 2, S-92.4)
clean.summary: Sheet 1 of 2 of standard drawing S-92.4 for a 14' cantilever standard carrying a changeable message sign up to 5'x12'. It shows the 8XX-Strong pipe post and arm elevation, the arm to post connection, the arm end plate and the 36" diameter, 12'-6" deep cast-in-drilled-hole foundation. Maximum sign weight is 750#, and numbered notes continue on sheet 2.
clean.notes:
Callouts: Sign arm 8XX-Strong pipe (max. sign weight = 750#). Post 8XX-Strong pipe. 5'X12' CMS (max.). 1" conduit to T. S. (traffic signal) pull box. Cast in drilled hole, 36" O.D. See Section A-A for reinforcing. Continuous 3/4" bar, see Note 1 (Details A and B).

The numbered notes referenced (Note 1) are not on this sheet and continue on sheet 2 of 2.

Approval: Approved on 11-21-05, Structural Engineering Division, Bureau of Engineering (BOE), by Peter Chiu.
clean.description:
Elevation: A 14' cantilever changeable message sign (CMS) standard. A vertical post of 8XX-Strong pipe carries a horizontal sign arm of 8XX-Strong pipe, with a 5'X12' CMS (max.) drawn as a dashed rectangle with break lines on the arm. The arm projects 14'-0" from the post centerline. The sign arm note reads max. sign weight = 750#. The post is 18" from top of post to arm centerline, 20'-1" from grade to arm centerline and 21'-7" from grade to post top (with break lines in the post). A 36" dimension locates the curb from the post centerline. A hand hole is shown low on the post. Detail "A" (arm to post connection, circled at the top), Detail "B" (arm end, circled at the end of the arm), Detail "C" (base, circled at grade) and Detail "D" (anchor bolt bottom plate) are called out. Below grade, a cast in drilled hole foundation 36" O.D. is 12'-6" deep with a 1" conduit to T. S. (traffic signal) pull box leaving it, 2'-0" MIN. below grade, see Section A-A for reinforcing.

Detail "A" (arm to post connection): Plan view shows the post, the sign arm, 1-1/4" and 1-1/4" plate dimensions, 1/4" and 1/2" welds, 1" x 1/4" backing ring, tack weld and 1/2" fillet weld. Elevation shows 3/16 pl. (removable top) 9-5/8" O.D. with 2 set screws, a bar 8" dia. x 2" x 3/16" bent to circular shape, a 1/8" weld, 18" dimension, 5/8" pl. x 4-3/8" x 14" long (2 required) with 1/2" weld, 4 - 1-1/2" dia. x 4" ASTM A325 bolts with hex nut and washer, sign arm 8-5/8" O.D. and post 8-5/8" O.D. A face view shows the connection plate with 4 - 1-1/2" dia. holes, 17" overall width with 13" hole spacing and 2" edge distances, 14" overall height with 10" hole spacing and 2" edge distances, R=2" corners, a 2" dia. hole, 3/4" std. half coupling, 5/8" x 5" x 9" long, 2 required, cut to fit flush, a 1/2" weld, a continuous 3/4" bar (see Note 1) with a 13/64" weld.

Detail "B" (arm end): An end plate 3/16" x 9" O.D. with a 1/8" weld on the arm end, a continuous 3/4" bar (see Note 1) with 13/64" weld inside the arm, shown in side and end views.

clean.title: 14' Cantilever Changeable Message Sign (Sheet 2 of 2, S-92.4)
clean.summary: Sheet 2 of 2 of standard drawing S-92.4 for the 14' cantilever changeable message sign standard. It gives the foundation reinforcing plan, the post base and anchor bolt detail, the anchor bar and the base weld, along with the 2001 AASHTO design basis, 85 mph wind velocity and seven general notes.
clean.notes:
Specifications. Design: 2001 American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials (AASHTO) Standard Specifications for structural supports for Highway Signs, Luminaires, and Traffic Signals. Wind velocity: 85 miles per hour (MPH).

General notes:
1. All pipes shall conform to ASTM A53 Grade B Specifications.
2. Bar reinforcements shall conform to ASTM A615, Grade 60.
3. All structural steel shall conform to ASTM designation A36, except as shown on the plan.
4. Welding design and fabrication shall be in accordance with the latest edition of the AWS Structural Welding Code D1.1-Steel.
5. All metal parts shall be galvanized after fabrication.
6. Sign Arm shall be made level by raking the standard with the leveling nuts or other method approved by the Engineer to compensate for dead load deflection.
7. Mounting Brackets shall be per Caltrans Standard Drawing No. S40R.

Detail callouts: Foundation concrete shall be 560-C-3250 (see reinf. in Sec. A-A).
clean.description:
Section A-A (plan of foundation): Circular cast in drilled hole foundation, 36" Dia., with 3" clear to the reinforcing. Shows 12-#7 x 9'-6" long bars equally spaced, #4 spiral @ 6" pitch, a base plate with 2" R corners and four anchor bolt holes in a 1'-1" by 1'-1" pattern (1'-6" overall plate width and height, 2-1/2" edge distances), a 3" dia. hole finished smooth at the center and a 2" dia. hole. The center line of the sign (CL Sign) is marked to the right.

Detail "C" (base of post and top of foundation): Section through the post base on the foundation. The post has a 3"x5" hand hole with frame and removable cover, 1" radius corners in hand hole, 4-1/2" and 8" dimensions above the base plate. The base plate is set at the top of walk on mortar with 2" and 2" dimensions, a 2'-8" overall dimension from the top of the plate to the bottom plate, and see Weld Detail. Callouts: 1" x 1/4" backing ring, tack weld, 3/8" dia. drain hole, 4 - 1-3/4" dia. anchor bolts, thrd. 8, galv. top 12", 2 hex nuts and 2 std. washers each, ASTM A-307, banding wire, 2" conduit, foundation concrete 560-C-3250 (see reinf. in Sec. A-A), and a bar 5" x 1" x 1'-7" long (parallel to axis of sign, 2 required) tack welded at the anchor bolt ends, 1" dimension at the bolt bottom. Section marker A points to Section A-A.

Detail "D" (anchor bar): Plan of the bar 5" wide, with two 1-7/8" dia. holes. Dimensions 3", 6-1/2", 6-1/2" and 3" along the length.

Weld Detail (not to scale): The pipe wall on the base plate with a backing ring and a tack weld, fillet weld shown 1/8 by 1/2 and a 1/2" dimension.

Specifications block: Design per 2001 AASHTO Standard Specifications for structural supports for Highway Signs, Luminaires, and Traffic Signals. Wind velocity 85 MPH.

clean.title: Trailblazer Sign (Sheet 1 of 2, S-58.16)
clean.summary: Sheet 1 of 2 of standard drawing S-58.16 for the freeway trailblazer sign. A 5' x 5' LED sign with FWY ALT and WEST or EAST legend, optionally paired with a 6' x 5' static Interstate 10 guide sign, is mounted on a cantilever pole with 12' arm per S-98.0. Layout dimensions of the LED legend are given, and the width can be increased by 12 inches for North or South.
clean.notes:
* Width can be increased by 12 inches to accommodate "North" or "South" legend.

Callouts: Installation per Std. Dwg. S-98.0. Unistrut installation (Detail "A"). Cantilever pole with 12' arm (Std. Dwg. S98.0). 1" flex conduit. Trailblazer LED sign. Static guide sign (optional).
clean.description:
Front view of LED legend faces (top of sheet): Two LED trailblazer sign faces are drawn, each a square outline 60" wide by 60" high (the left one is marked *60", the asterisk referring to the width footnote). The left face shows the legend FWY ALT on the top line and an arrow pointing left, an arrow pointing up, and WEST on the bottom line, made of dot (LED) characters. The right face shows FWY ALT on the top line and EAST followed by a right arrow on the bottom line. On each face the vertical layout is 13" top margin, 10" high top line of text, 14" gap, 10" high bottom line of text, 13" bottom margin (total 60").

Rear view (not to scale): Two sign cabinets side by side, one 5' wide plus one 6' wide, mounted on a horizontal cantilever arm which comes off a vertical cantilever pole at the left, labeled Cantilever Pole with 12' Arm (Std. Dwg. S98.0). Installation per Std. Dwg. S-98.0 is noted at the arm connection points. Four Unistrut installation (Detail "A") members run vertically across the two panels, and the arm is shown ending 1' Max. from the right edge of the sign. A 1" flex conduit loops from the arm end downward. Panel height is 5'.

Front view (not to scale): Two signs side by side on the arm. The left sign is the Trailblazer LED Sign, 5' wide (*5') by 5' high, with the legend FWY ALT over an arrow pointing left, an up arrow and WEST. The right sign is a Static Guide Sign (optional), 6' wide by 5' high, with an Interstate 10 shield at the top, a large left arrow and FWY. The pole is at the right of the front view with a short stub arm. A 1' Max. dimension is shown at the left side of the front view.

Footnote: * Width can be increased by 12 inches to accommodate "North" or "South" legend.

(Not To Scale) Pipe Clamps O.D. 6 5/8” Thickness: 11Ga Design Load 100 Ibs Traiblazer signs to be used in conjunction with static freeway overhead guide signs. Use one or two arrows on the trailblazer sign as appropriate. Sign shall utilize Light Emitting Diodes (LED) for message illumination. The individual LED’s shall equal or exceed in quality as those manufactured by Hewlett-Packard, high power ALInGAP amber type, catalog #HLMA—DLOO. Sign text shall be 10” U.C. with 1” spacing between each letter and a minimum of one letter width spacing between words. The overall sign size shall be 60” in height x 60” in width and 8” in depth. The weight of the sign (enclosure + all components) shall not exceed 115 Ibs. The sign shall be constructed so that the front face panel shall be contained within an extruded 0.90 aluminum frame having full welded seams and powder coat painted with high gloss black finish meeting the color standards of Fed. Spec. 595b, 17038. The transparent Lexan front face panel shall be hinged at the top allowing front access to the interior of the sign. Support shall be provided to hold the Lexan panel open during maintenance. A honeycomb formed black anodized screen shall be provided between the LED’s lamp clusters and the front face panel to enhance resistance to "sun phantom” effect. The sign shall use a closed cell neoprene gasket making the sign watertight. Sign enclosure hardware materials shall be stainless steel AISI303, for corrosion resitance. An opening shall be made on the bottom side of the sign so that all conductors, enclosed in flexible conduit, may exit from the sign into the cantilever arm. The sign shall be vented in the bottom portion on the opposite end from the conductor opening. The LED elements shall be comprised of individual removable modules. Each LED modules shall be composed of 1” pixels (clusters) having 8 each LED’s per pixel. One module shall be used for each letter of the message. Each pixel shall be removable or replaceable on the module without the use of any tools other than a screwdriver. The sign shall be equipped with a photoelectric cell mounted on the enclosure to measure ambient light intensity and automatically compensate for ambient light conditions. The LED sign shall be mountable using unistrut mounting system. Sign shall be equipped with a terminal block to provide separate power inputs to each of the text and arrow modules. The sign shall be powered with 120V AC. A full set of proposed sign specifications and drawings shall be supplied to the City prior to manufacturing. clean.notes:

8. The transparent Lexan front face panel shall be hinged at the top allowing front access to the interior of the sign. Support shall be provided to hold the Lexan panel open during maintenance.
9. A honeycomb formed black anodized screen shall be provided between the LED's lamp clusters and the front face panel to enhance resistance to "sun phantom" effect.
10. The sign shall use a closed cell neoprene gasket making the sign watertight.
11. Sign enclosure hardware materials shall be stainless steel AISI303, for corrosion resistance.
12. An opening shall be made on the bottom side of the sign so that all conductors, enclosed in flexible conduit, may exit from the sign into the cantilever arm.
13. The sign shall be vented in the bottom portion on the opposite end from the conductor opening.

15. Each pixel shall be removable or replaceable on the module without the use of any tools other than a screwdriver.
16. The sign shall be equipped with a photoelectric cell mounted on the enclosure to measure ambient light intensity and automatically compensate for ambient light conditions.
17. The LED sign shall be mountable using unistrut mounting system.
18. Sign shall be equipped with a terminal block to provide separate power inputs to each of the text and arrow modules. The sign shall be powered with 120V AC.

USE SELF LOCKING NUTS ON NON-HIGH STRENGTH (H.S.) BOLTS, UNLESS OTHERWISE SHOWN OR SPECIFIED. FOUNDATION DESIGN IS BASED ON BROMS' METHOD ASSUMING A COHESIVE SOIL WITH AN UNDRAINED SHEAR STRENGTH OF 1.50 KSF WITH A FACTOR OF SAFETY OF 3.0. PILE LENGTHS SHALL BE INCREASED BY AN AMOUNT EQUAL TO THE THICKNESS OF ANY EXISTING FILL SOILS ENCOUNTERED AT THE SIGN LOCATION DURING CONSTRUCTION. clean.title: Overhead Sign Structure Standard Drawings, Monotube Cantilever Sign (S-99.0, Sheet S-1 of 5)
clean.summary: Sheet S-1 of 5 of LADOT Standard Drawing S-99.0, 2011, for monotube cantilever overhead signs up to 40'-0" long and 6'-0" high. It shows the support plan and elevation (20'-0" clear, 25'-0" max post), a tube selection table for three structure sizes, typical arm and post sections, the sheet index and the design, material, bolting, galvanizing and foundation notes.
clean.notes:
General notes:
Design:
- Sign support structures designed in accordance with AASHTO Standard Specifications for Structural Support for Highway Signs, Luminaires and Traffic Signals: 5th edition.
- Sign weight used for sign support structure design is 3 psf.
- Basic wind speed (3 second gust) used for sign support structures design is 100 MPH, G = 1.14, I = 1.0 (50 year recurrence interval).
- Fatigue importance factor, I_f = 1.0, used for fatigue design of sign support structures considering galloping, natural wind gust and truck-induced gust.
- Pipe members shall conform to ASTM A53 GR. B.
- HSS tube members shall conform to ASTM A500 GR. B.
- All other structural steel shall conform to ASTM A36, or A992, unless noted otherwise.
- Welding shall be in conformance with the latest edition of AWS - D1.1 Structural Welding Code.
- Notch toughness of all structural steel members and plates greater than 1/2" thick shall conform to Zone 2 requirements of AASHTO M270M/M270 supplementary requirement S5 (ASTM A709/A709M, supplementary requirement S83).
- High strength bolts shall conform to ASTM A325, Type 1.
- Nuts for high strength bolts shall be heavy hex and conform to ASTM A563 Grade DH, with supplementary requirements "S1" and "S2".
- Hardened steel washers shall conform to ASTM F436, Type 1. Use washers under turning element in tightening unless otherwise specified.
- All fasteners shall be hot-dip galvanized.
- All structural steel shall be hot-dip galvanized after fabrication, unless noted otherwise.
- The silicon content of the base metal shall be in the ranges of 0.0% to 0.04% or 0.15% to 0.25% for all hot-dip galvanized steel, unless noted otherwise.
- All H.S. bolts shall be considered slip critical unless noted otherwise. Design slip resistance for bolts shall conform to the bolt specifications for Class C slip coefficient = 0.33.
- Use self locking nuts on non-high strength (H.S.) bolts, unless otherwise shown or specified.
- Foundation design is based on Broms' method assuming a cohesive soil with an undrained shear strength of 1.50 ksf with a factor of safety of 3.0.
- Pile lengths shall be increased by an amount equal to the thickness of any existing fill soils encountered at the sign location during construction.
- Bureau of Engineering's Geotechnical Engineering Group (213-847-0538) shall be contacted for recommendations if weak soils and/or groundwater is encountered during construction of the CIDH (cast-in-drilled-hole) piles.
- All concrete shall be class 3600.
- All reinforcing steel shall conform to ASTM A706 or A615 GR. 60.
- Anchor rods shall conform to ASTM F1554, GR. 55, with supplementary requirement "S4" (AASHTO M314). Top ends of anchor rods shall be ground flat at 90 degrees to rod axis. Final surface roughness shall not exceed 125 micro-inch.
- Anchor rod washers shall conform to ASTM F436.
- Anchor rod nuts shall conform to ASTM A563 GR. DH with supplementary requirements "S1" and "S2".
- Anchor rods shall be hot-dip galvanized full length.

Plan callouts: 40'-0" MAX sign length; 6'-0" MAX sign height and support spacing; 2'-6" MAX; 20'-0" CLEAR; 25'-0" MAX; centroid of sign area; level.
clean.description:
Sheet S-1 of 5 of Standard Drawing S-99.0, a large-format LADOT sheet with four views, an index, general notes and the title block.

Detail I1, Cantilever sign support plan (top view of the arm layout, scale 1/4" = 1'-0", reference S-1): A horizontal line of sign frame supports (vertical stiffeners) at a maximum spacing of 6'-0" MAX along the sign, drawn above a traffic edge line with a TRAFFIC arrow. The sign is shown as a long rectangle of vertical members over the arm, ending at a post at the right with the curb line 3'-0" from the post centerline. The arm runs along the sign and the post is drawn as a circle with a U-shaped bracket at the right end.

Cantilever sign support plan (lower plan view): The sign is up to 40'-0" MAX long and 6'-0" MAX high. The distance from the free end of the sign to the first support is 2'-6" MAX. Dimension C is the offset of the arm from the sign edge, with the arm drawn dashed, labeled LEVEL, SIGN and ARM. A long dimension line to the centerline (CL) at the post and centroid of sign area are marked. Reference callouts: A1 on S-3 (arm connection), G11 on S-4, I1 on S-3, and section cut A on S-2. The post stands at the right end with a flange, shown circled.

C1, Cantilever sign support elevation (scale 1/4" = 1'-0", S-1): The post is a vertical tube, 25'-0" MAX from grade to the arm top, with the sign bottom 20'-0" CLEAR above the roadway. The curb line is 3'-0" from the post centerline, and the pile foundation below is 3'-0" wide (circled D1, on S-5). Two anchor details labeled G11 (S-4) and J1 (S-4) are shown at the base with 3'-0" and 2'-0" vertical dimensions. The post has labels SIGN, ARM, POST and CURB LINE.

A1, Tube selection table (NTS, S-1): columns Structure No., Sign Length, Max CL, Max Sign Area, Dp, tp, Wa, ta, Ra, C.
Structure 1: sign length 10'-20', max CL 16'-0", max sign area 120 FT2, Dp 1'-6", tp 1/2", Wa 1'-4", ta 1/2", Ra 2-1/2", C 3".
Structure 2: sign length 20'-30', max CL 21'-0", max sign area 180 FT2, Dp 2'-0", tp 1/2", Wa 1'-10", ta 1/2", Ra 2-1/2", C 4-1/4".
Structure 3: sign length 30'-40', max CL 26'-0", max sign area 240 FT2, Dp 2'-6", tp 5/8", Wa 2'-4", ta 1/2", Ra 2-1/2", C 5".

A8, Typ arm section (scale 3/4" = 1'-0", S-1): A square tube arm section with width Wa each way, wall thickness ta and corner radius Ra.

A12, Typ post section (scale 3/4" = 1'-0", S-1): A round tube post with outside diameter Dp and wall thickness tp.

Index to sheets: Sheet 1, S-1, Monotube cantilever sign. Sheet 2, S-2, Tubular structural frame details - 1. Sheet 3, S-3, Tubular structural frame details - 2. Sheet 4, S-4, Tubular base plate and anchorage details. Sheet 5, S-5, Round pedestal pile foundation.
